Position Overview

WD is seeking a Chief of Staff to serve as a strategic partner and operational advisor jointly supporting the VP of Business Applications and the VP of Digital Employee Experience. This role sits at the intersection of two complementary IT organizations, connecting strategy to execution across both portfolios and ensuring the combined leadership team operates with shared clarity, alignment, and accountability.

The Chief of Staff works alongside both VP leaders to drive organizational priorities forward, maintain operational rhythm, and represent IT interests across cross-functional forums. Given the dual scope of this role, the ability to hold context across multiple domains, balance competing priorities thoughtfully, and build trust with two distinct leadership teams is essential. This is a high-visibility, high-trust role that requires sound judgment, executive presence, strong communication instincts, and the ability to operate effectively across a complex, matrixed global technology organization.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Strategic Enablement & Organizational Leadership

  • Partner with both the VP of Business Applications and the VP of Digital Employee Experience to develop, refine, and communicate IT strategic priorities across their respective organizations and to shared stakeholders

  • Translate strategy across both IT portfolios into actionable roadmaps, plans, and organizational commitments

  • Serve as a thought partner to both VP leaders on organizational decisions, planning trade-offs, and priority setting

  • Help identify opportunities for alignment, synergy, and shared execution across the Business Applications and Digital Employee Experience organizations

  • Represent both VP leadership interests in cross-functional forums, planning sessions, and executive reviews as appropriate

  • Help shape and steward the IT organizational narrative across both domains, ensuring consistent messaging for internal and external audiences

Operational Execution & Cadence

  • Own the operating cadence across both IT organizations, including leadership team rhythms, QBRs, strategic planning cycles, and technology reviews

  • Drive accountability across both leadership teams for key commitments, deliverables, and milestones

  • Proactively identify and resolve operational blockers, escalating or connecting stakeholders where needed

  • Maintain visibility into initiative portfolios across both organizations, surfacing risks, dependencies, and progress for leadership review

  • Identify and improve operational processes that span or connect the two IT organizations to increase overall efficiency and effectiveness

Decision Support & Executive Communications

  • Synthesize complex information from across both IT organizations and the broader business to inform leadership decisions and recommendations

  • Lead development of executive presentations, strategic briefings, and business updates on behalf of both VP leaders

  • Translate technical and operational content into clear, compelling narratives for business and executive audiences

  • Prepare both VP leaders for high-stakes meetings, technology reviews, and partner forums

  • Manage strategic communications flowing from both IT organizations to internal teams and business partners

Financial & Resource Planning Partnership

  • Partner with Finance to ensure budget planning, forecasting, and expense management processes across both IT organizations are well-coordinated and accurately represented to leadership

  • Maintain leadership-level visibility into headcount, resource allocation, and workforce planning across both portfolios in partnership with HR

  • Support both VP leaders in making informed resource prioritization decisions aligned with organizational strategy and demand

  • Track and flag material variances in budget or resource plans across either organization with appropriate context and recommended actions

Performance Visibility & Insights

  • Oversee tracking and reporting of key performance indicators spanning both the Business Applications and Digital Employee Experience portfolios

  • Ensure both VP leaders have timely, accurate, and actionable visibility into organizational performance through consolidated dashboards and scorecards

  • Identify performance trends, risks, and opportunities across both organizations and bring them forward with context and perspective

  • Drive consistent, high-quality reporting practices across both IT organizations

Cross-Functional Coordination & Stakeholder Alignment

  • Serve as a primary coordination point bridging Business Applications, Digital Employee Experience, and other IT domains including Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, and Enterprise Architecture

  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with key business partner organizations including Finance, HR, Supply Chain, and Operations

  • Facilitate alignment across shared IT priorities, service commitments, and technology roadmaps that span both VP organizations

  • Help navigate organizational complexity and resolve cross-functional friction points on behalf of both VP leaders

Organizational Health & Culture

  • Contribute to a healthy, high-performing culture across both IT organizations by modeling clarity, accountability, and inclusion in day-to-day operations

  • Support both VP leaders in communication efforts that keep their respective organizations informed, engaged, and connected to strategy

  • Help identify and address organizational gaps, team dynamics, and structural issues that may affect effectiveness across either portfolio

  • Champion continuous improvement across IT ways of working, team collaboration, and shared organizational practices

Special Projects & Strategic Initiatives

  • Lead or co-lead high-priority special projects on behalf of either or both VP leaders

  • Support transformation and modernization initiatives across both IT portfolios through research, analysis, coordination, and stakeholder engagement

  • Take end-to-end ownership of defined strategic workstreams from scoping through delivery

  • Provide analytical and strategic support for emerging priorities and leadership agenda items across both organizations

Scope & Impact

  • Operates as a direct extension of two IT VP leaders across strategic and operational matters spanning Business Applications and Digital Employee Experience

  • Regular engagement with VP and C-suite-level stakeholders across IT and the broader business

  • Cross-functional reach spanning multiple IT domains and major business partner organizations

  • Meaningful influence over how two distinct but complementary IT organizations operate, communicate, and deliver on shared and individual commitments across the enterprise

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business, Computer Science, Finance, or a related field

  • 8 or more years of progressive experience in IT strategy, IT operations, business operations, chief of staff, or senior program leadership roles

  • Demonstrated ability to operate effectively at the VP or executive level in a complex, matrixed organization

  • Proven ability to manage and balance competing priorities across multiple stakeholders and organizational contexts simultaneously

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with a track record of executive-level storytelling and presentation development

  • Strong analytical capability with experience synthesizing data into strategic recommendations

  • Sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to handle sensitive organizational information with care

  • Proven ability to manage multiple competing priorities with composure and clarity in a fast-paced environment

Preferred

  • Experience in a formal Chief of Staff, Senior Director of Strategy, or equivalent advisory role within an enterprise IT organization

  • Background in technology, manufacturing, semiconductor, or related industries

  • Familiarity with IT financial management, portfolio planning, and vendor management practices

  • Experience supporting multiple VP or C-suite leaders concurrently within a global organization

  • Exposure to IT strategic planning, digital transformation, and organizational change management

  • Knowledge of ITIL, Agile, or related IT service and delivery frameworks

  • MBA or advanced degree strongly preferred

raw.description:
The Quantitative Research Operations Manager is a technical, behind-the-scenes role responsible for supporting the execution and quality of the organization's quantitative research.

You will work across studies to ensure surveys are programmed correctly, data is clean and accurate, and reporting outputs are client-ready. This includes program checking, data scanning and cleaning, data processing, report population, and rigorous numerical QC.

This is an ideal role for someone who enjoys the technical and operational side of quantitative research, has exceptional attention to detail, and naturally notices when something in the data doesn’t look right.

Duties and Responsibilities

Survey Programming & QA

  • Review programmed surveys against questionnaires for accuracy and consistency
  • Test survey logic, skips, piping, randomization, quotas, calculations, and respondent flow
  • Conduct soft-launch data checks and identify potential programming or fieldwork issues
  • Partner with researchers and programming vendors to troubleshoot and resolve issues

Data Quality & Processing

  • Scan and clean respondent-level data throughout fieldwork and at study close
  • Identify poor-quality respondents, inconsistent responses, suspicious open ends, speeders, straightliners, and other data-quality concerns
  • Investigate unexpected data patterns and troubleshoot potential programming, sampling, or data-processing issues
  • Support recodes, derived variables, banners, crosstabs, weighting, and significance testing
  • Review data tables and other outputs for accuracy and consistency

Reporting & Analysis Support

  • Populate PowerPoint reports with survey data, including charts and tables
  • Check bases, percentages, significance, calculations, and data labels
  • Conduct rigorous numerical QC of client deliverables
  • Troubleshoot discrepancies across raw data, tables, and reporting outputs
  • Prepare clean, analysis-ready data and outputs for research teams

Operational Excellence

  • Serve as a centralized resource for quantitative research quality and technical execution
  • Develop and improve standardized processes for program checking, data cleaning, reporting, and QC
  • Identify opportunities to automate or streamline repetitive quantitative workflows
  • Learn and leverage AI-powered tools and platforms to improve efficiency and quality

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree (market research, psychology, sociology, business, communications, or related field preferred)
  • 0–2 years of experience (internships count)
  • High attention to detail
  • Strong analytical and writing skills
  • Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint (experience with survey or analytics tools a plus)
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines in a remote environment

raw.description:
Twin Health

At Twin Health, we empower people to improve and prevent chronic metabolic diseases, like type 2 diabetes and obesity, with a new standard of care. Twin Health is the only company applying AI Digital Twin technology exclusively toward metabolic health.

We start by building a dynamic model of each person’s metabolism — drawing on thousands of data points from CGMs, smartwatches, and meal logs — that maps their personal path to better health. Guided by a dedicated clinical care team, our members have lowered their A1C below the diabetes range, achieved lasting weight loss, and reduced or even eliminated medications, all while living healthier, happier lives.

Working here

Our team at Twin Health is passionate, talented, and united by a shared purpose: to improve the metabolic health and happiness of our members. We believe in empowering every Twin to make a meaningful impact for our members, our clients, and each other, while enjoying a supportive, collaborative work environment.

Twin has been recognized not only for our innovation but also for our culture, including: Innovator of the Year by the Employer Health Innovation Roundtable (EHIR), selected to CB Insights’ Digital Health 150, and named one of Newsweek’s Top Most Loved Workplace® .

With more than $100 million raised in recent funding, including a $53 million Series E round in 2025 led by Maj Invest, and a $50 million investment in 2023 led by Temasek, Twin is scaling rapidly across the U.S. and globally. Backed by leading venture firms like ICONIQ Growth, Sequoia, Sofina, Temasek, and Peak XV, we are building the most impactful digital health company in the world.

Join us as we reinvent the standard of care in metabolic health.

Opportunity

Twin is looking for a Creative Director, Copy to lead the voice behind everything Twin writes, both for members reversing and preventing disease and for the employers, health plans, and consultants who buy the platform for them. You'll report to the Sr. Director, Brand & Experience and own Twin's written voice end to end: setting the standard, building the system that lets a growing team write in it consistently, and stepping in personally on the highest-stakes copy that carries the brand at its biggest moments.

This is a player-coach role, and it's a leadership role: you'll be one of two direct leads under the Sr. Director, Brand & Experience (the other leading Design), and you'll act as that leader's delegate and backup on brand voice and copy decisions. You'll directly lead a small, growing writing team (a Member writer, a B2B writer, and a flexible B2B/B2C support writer) while also being a hands-on writer yourself for Twin's most visible moments: brand manifestos, executive-level messaging, and the pieces where getting the voice right matters most.

Responsibilities

  • Own Twin's voice and tone across every audience (member, employer, health plan, broker/consultant, unions) and keep the Voice & Language Guide alive as the team and the brand evolve.
  • Act as Twin's narrative through-line: the steward who catches it when a piece of content is technically on-brief but doesn't actually hold up, and who prevents narrative drift as the company and the team scale.
  • Own the overarching content calendar for brand and editorial voice across all channels and audiences so there's a single point of editorial visibility across everything shipping, not just what the direct writing team produces.
  • Apply a structured editorial plan to significant content before it ships: audience, goal, narrative arc (opening/middle/close), optimization approach, and key points, not just a final voice pass.
  • Lead, mentor, and grow Twin's copywriters (Member and B2B), building their judgment so they can make brand-right calls independently, not just execute a brief.
  • Distribute workload and priorities across the writing team as it grows, so no single writer is the bottleneck for an entire audience.
  • Write and edit personally where the brand's voice is most exposed: brand manifestos, executive thought leadership, and campaign centerpieces.
  • Partner with the Sr. Director, Brand & Experience and Product Marketing to translate brand strategy and positioning into copy standards the team can execute against, and serve as their delegate on voice/copy decisions when needed.
  • Operate as the cross-functional owner that other teams (Product Marketing, BD/Sales, and campaign owners, including brand and social content) route content through for a final voice and coherence check, without needing direct authority over their teams to make that work.
  • Review and elevate the team's work before it ships: the difference between technically on-brief and sounding like Twin.
  • A shared creative remit with the design leadership counterpart (Senior Design Creative/ACD), and weigh in on the visual system, not just the words, so copy and design ship as one holistic voice, one look and feel, not two separate reviews.
  • Build repeatable systems (style guides, review workflows, onboarding for new writers) so quality doesn't depend on any one person's memory.
  • Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

  • 7+ years in copywriting or content strategy, including experience leading or mentoring other writers — with a meaningful percentage of that in healthcare, health tech, or another complex, regulated buyer environment (benefits, fintech, etc.), where you've had to write with the support and approval of a clinical/legal review
  • A portfolio that shows real range — consumer/emotional writing and B2B/executive writing
  • Experience translating brand strategy and voice guidelines into a working system a team can execute against, not just a personal style.
  • Comfortable as both a working writer and a people leader — this role edits and writes, it doesn't only manage.
  • Strong judgment on when to hold the line on brand voice and when to flex for audience or channel.
  • Experience driving alignment and quality across teams you don't directly manage — getting Product Marketing, BD, and campaign owners to route content through you without it feeling like a bottleneck.
  • Experience partnering cross-functionally with Product Marketing, Design, and clinical/legal reviewers on regulated or claims-sensitive content.
  • Comfortable operating as a leadership-team delegate — able to represent brand voice decisions on someone else's behalf, not just your own work.
  • Bonus Skills
  • Experience building or running a formal brand voice/style guide.
  • Executive ghostwriting or founder-voice experience.
  • Familiarity with claims/clinical review processes in a regulated industry.
  • Experience mentoring writers from junior to senior levels.
  • This remote opportunity based out of the U.S. Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time.

Compensation and Benefits

The compensation range for this position is $190,000 - $205,000 annually.

Twin has an ambitious vision to empower people to live healthier and happier lives, and to achieve this purpose, we need the very best people to enhance our cutting-edge technology and medical science, deliver the best possible care, and turn our passion into value for our members, partners and investors. We are committed to delivering an outstanding culture and experience for every Twin employee through a company based on the values of passion, talent, and trust. We offer comprehensive benefits and perks in line with these principles, as well as a high level of flexibility for every Twin

  • A competitive compensation package in line with leading technology companies
  • A remote and accomplished global team
  • Opportunity for equity participation
  • Unlimited vacation with manager approval
  • 16 weeks of 100% paid parental leave for delivering parents; 8 weeks of 100% paid parental leave for non-delivering parents
  • 100% Employer sponsored healthcare, dental, and vision for you, and 80% coverage for your family; Health Savings Account and Flexible Spending Account options

Our team develops the GPU-accelerated libraries and SDKs essential for these technologies.

At LearnWorlds, we believe learning is the original human superpower, the force that turns knowledge into products, skills, and progress.

Our platform helps creators, educators, and organizations in more than 150 countries turn expertise into scalable learning experiences that sell, teach, and transform. As AI floods the world with information, learning becomes the only countermeasure, the skill that keeps humans creative, relevant, and in control.

The winners won't be those who automate fastest, but those who learn and adapt fastest. They'll need platforms that turn knowledge into teachable systems that scale, and that's exactly what LearnWorlds enables.

Build. Ship. Test. Improve. (Repeat.)

We're redefining how people create and share online learning and we're doing it with engineers who care deeply about product quality, clean architecture, and meaningful impact. We're a remote-first, fast-growing EdTech SaaS with a global footprint.

Our Engineering team builds the core experiences that thousands of educators and learners rely on daily. We move fast, we collaborate tightly, and we're constantly leveling up, both as individuals and as a team.

We're now looking for an experienced Software Engineer in Test to own automation outcomes for assigned product areas. You will build and maintain reliable Playwright and TypeScript automated tests using the Page Object Model (POM) pattern, and help teams decide what should be automated and what should stay manual or exploratory. You'll direct AI Agents daily to plan, generate, debug and maintain automation. It's how the work ships here, not a perk.

You'll join an established and fast-paced environment with a focus on ensuring quality deliveries and exceptional experience to all our users.

If you're a engineer who loves solving real quality challenges, writing maintainable test code, directing AI agents with judgment, and building automation that teams actually trust, this is where you'll do your best work.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own your product area. Join planning before the code exists, while scope, risk, data, and environments are still cheap to change
  • Pick the right layer. API where it's enough, E2E where only a browser will do, smoke for release signal, the cheapest test that still catches the bug
  • Build and evolve the framework. Page objects, flows, typed API clients, fixtures, code other engineers read and extend
  • Work across Product and Engineering. Push for testability while the design is still open, and keep automation useful instead of noisy
  • Design Phase. Formulate efficient and deterministic test scenarios and create comprehensive test strategy plans
  • Own CI e2e. Fast, deterministic, diagnosable. Fix flakiness at the root cause; a rerun is not a fix.
  • Report coverage and risk honestly. What automation covers, what it doesn't, and what still needs manual or exploratory testing.
  • Report defects developers can act on. Identify, categorize, and report bugs and errors to development teams with insightful information (screenshots, traces, error messages, stack traces, etc.), separating product defects from automation defects, environment issues, and data problems
  • Direct AI Agents, then own the output. Plan scope, generate tests, investigate failures and reject what's flaky, unasserted, or five times larger than the task.
  • Build the AI tooling layer. Reusable agent skills, subagent definitions, and the machine-readable convention rules everyone's tests get reviewed against locators, page-object structure, spec placement, test IDs, so generated tests are correct by default.
  • Shape the testing standards, don't just follow them.

Why You'll Love This Role

  • You'll work on real features used by thousands of educators and, most importantly, tens of millions of learners around the world
  • You'll build and evolve test automation that scales with our growing platform and ensures quality at every release
  • You'll be part of a tight-knit team where your ideas matter, and your work directly impacts product quality
  • You'll grow fast—technically and professionally in a team that's generous with knowledge and big on collaboration
  • You'll own meaningful product-area automation, not just isolated test cases, and help teams ship faster
  • You'll work in an engineering culture that treats Agentic AI as a real skill: prompt, steer, review, and ship faster without lowering the bar for test quality

Requirements

Must-Haves

  • At least 3 years of professional experience as a Quality Assurance / Software Testing engineer, with strong automation ownership
  • Strong proficiency in TypeScript and modern JavaScript/TypeScript development practices
  • Hands-on experience with Playwright test automation framework (or a comparable modern web automation framework) and Page Object Model (POM) design pattern
  • Experience with version control systems (Git) and CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions or similar)
  • Excellent analytical thinking to produce and document test scenarios, acceptance criteria, and test strategy plans
  • Comfortable at more than one layer, API, UI, cross-browser, responsive, and able to say which one a given risk belongs to
  • Excellent debugging, problem-solving, and performance optimization skills
  • Close attention to detail and a product-oriented mindset, automation is a tool for product confidence, not the goal by itself
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts, coverage, gaps, and remaining risk
  • Team player with the ability to get things done in a non-hierarchical flat organization
  • Excellent prioritization, estimation, and scheduling skills
  • Ability to learn the LearnWorlds platform quickly and connect automation decisions to real customer workflows
  • Proven Agentic AI skills: you regularly use and improve AI agents to complete multi-step test engineering work—planning, generating, debugging, and maintaining automation
  • Strong judgment over AI output: you review, steer, and reject generated tests that are flaky, insecure, poorly structured, or disconnected from real risk

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, or containerized test environments
  • Experience in EdTech, LMS systems, payments, ecommerce, analytics, mobile, or other complex SaaS products
  • Experience with test management tools (TestRail, Zephyr, or similar)
  • Familiarity with cloud technologies like AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud
  • Experience with backend/API automation beyond UI flows
  • GitHub repos, open-source contributions, or personal projects you're proud of

You'll Thrive Here If You…

  • Prefer ownership over hand-holding and clarity over bureaucracy
  • Think speed and quality can (and should) co-exist
  • Ask "why" before "how," and make decisions with context, not just checklists
  • Love clean code, good architecture, and continuous improvement
  • Embrace feedback, stay curious, and enjoy sharing knowledge
  • Treat AI agents as collaborators you direct with clear intent, not as a shortcut around engineering judgment
  • Believe AI won't replace QA engineers—but engineers who work well with agents will outperform those who don't

Benefits

    • Your personal annual training budget
    • An annual home office allowance to set up your personal space

raw.excerpt: About TelnyxTelnyx is an industry leader that's not just imagining the future of global connectivity—we're building it.
raw.description:
About Telnyx

Telnyx is an industry leader that's not just imagining the future of global connectivity—we're building it. From architecting and amplifying the reach of a private, global, multi-cloud IP network, to bringing hyperlocal edge technology right to your fingertips through intuitive APIs, we're shaping a new era of seamless interconnection between people, devices, and applications.

We're driven by a desire to transform and modernize what's antiquated, automate the manual, and solve real-world problems through innovative connectivity solutions. As a testament to our success, we're proud to stand as a financially stable and profitable company. Our robust profitability allows us not only to invest in pioneering technologies but also to foster an environment of continuous learning and growth for our team.

Our collective vision is a world where borderless connectivity fuels limitless innovation. By joining us, you can be part of laying the foundations for this interconnected future. We're currently seeking passionate individuals who are excited about the opportunity to contribute to an industry-shaping company while growing their own skills and careers.

Inference Infrastructure Architect
Senior / Staff · Remote — mainland China · Founding China team

Telnyx runs its own B300 fleet — our hardware, in our facilities, operated from the metal up, and expanding globally. This role exists to turn that fleet into useful throughput: Telnyx's own AI-agent traffic on the voice and messaging network, and external customers' inference behind the token gateway, dedicated deployments and tuned models.

You have two mandates:

  1. Operate and expand the fleet efficiently. Maximize useful inference throughput per GPU-dollar while meeting latency and reliability SLOs, and continuously reduce cost per token.
  2. Make the product run on it. Serverless inference for the open-weight catalog, and dedicated, tuned model deployments for enterprises.

The stack is open source, bare metal to OpenAI-compatible endpoint. You work upstream in it.

What you'll build

  • Serverless serving pools. vLLM / SGLang engines with continuous batching, prefix caching, low-precision serving (FP8, FP4, INT4) and MoE expert parallelism, serving the head of the open-weight catalog at multi-tenant scale.
  • The fleet layer. llm-d / NVIDIA Dynamo on the Kubernetes Gateway API: KV-cache-aware routing, prefill/decode disaggregation, KV tiering (Mooncake), and multi-LoRA serving so hundreds of customer adapters share one base pool.
  • The platform under it. Kubernetes on bare metal: GPU Operator, topology-aware scheduling, LeaderWorkerSet, Kueue; Kata Containers for isolated dedicated tenants; bare-metal lifecycle with OpenStack Ironic.
  • Weight logistics and elasticity. P2P model distribution (Dragonfly, safetensors streaming), warm pools, and autoscaling driven by inference metrics — queue depth, KV occupancy, TTFT — never CPU.
  • The dedicated tier. Per-tenant pools, GPU-hour metering, latency SLOs, private networking; and the serving side of the model-tuning loop: adapter versioning, canary rollout, rollback on outcome regression.
  • Observability and economics. DCGM and engine metrics into Prometheus / OpenTelemetry; capacity planning grounded in roofline math — bandwidth-bound decode, batching curves, utilization versus cost per token.

The stack you'll work in

Some of this is committed direction: Kubernetes on bare metal, vLLM / SGLang, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Much of the rest is candidates you'll evaluate. You'll select, benchmark and integrate the components that earn their place in production. We value depth in the core serving stack and sound architectural judgment, not prior experience with every project listed.

  • Engines: vLLM · SGLang
  • Serving techniques: prefill/decode disaggregation · wide expert parallelism · speculative decoding (MTP, EAGLE-3) · low precision (FP8, FP4, INT4)
  • MoE & attention libraries: DeepEP · DeepGEMM · EPLB · FlashMLA
  • Routing & serving: llm-d · NVIDIA Dynamo · Kubernetes Gateway API · Envoy · Ray Serve / KubeRay
  • KV cache & weights: Mooncake · HiCache · 3FS · Dragonfly
  • Scheduling & GPU sharing: Kubernetes · Volcano · Kueue · LeaderWorkerSet · HAMi
  • Isolation & bare metal: Kata Containers · OpenStack Ironic · NVIDIA GPU Operator
  • Observability: Prometheus · Grafana · DCGM · OpenTelemetry

What we look for

  • You have owned production LLM serving under meaningful traffic and latency constraints, and can explain the architecture, the bottlenecks you diagnosed, the changes you made, and the resulting improvements in latency, reliability or cost. Scale on the order of thousands of GPUs or millions of requests a day is a strong signal, not a hard requirement.
  • Kubernetes on GPU fleets, operated end to end: GPU Operator, device plugins, node pools and topology-aware placement, gang scheduling (LeaderWorkerSet, Kueue), GitOps rollouts, and the ability to debug why a pod landed where it did.
  • Deep operational command of vLLM or SGLang: deploying, tuning and upgrading it (parallelism with TP / EP, quantization, batch and KV-cache settings, prefix caching, disaggregation), and knowing which knob moves which metric.
  • Performance engineering at the system level: you read engine and DCGM metrics, reason from roofline, and size deployments with numbers.
  • Python and Go for automation; real Linux, networking and storage depth. You don't need to write CUDA; you need to know when a problem is one, and route it upstream.
  • You work with the community in English and Chinese, and write runbooks and design docs people actually read.

Experience we especially value

  • Operated inference platforms at the scale of Ant Group, Alibaba Cloud / PAI, Tencent, ByteDance, Baidu, Huawei, DaoCloud, Moonshot, DeepSeek, or comparable teams.
  • Contributor to, or heavy production user of, any of: vLLM, SGLang, llm-d, NVIDIA Dynamo, Ray / KubeRay, Kata Containers, Volcano, Kueue, HAMi, Dragonfly, Mooncake, Envoy.
  • Presence in the CNCF / OpenInfra community: talks at KubeCon China, OpenInfra Days, vLLM or SGLang meetups.

Nice to have

  • Fine-tuning / RL infrastructure: LoRA pipelines, evaluation harnesses, champion/challenger rollout.
  • Real-time voice latency work: sub-second time-to-first-token budgets on live calls.
  • Multi-region deployments and data-residency requirements.

What we offer

  • The newest hardware, ours from the metal up. A globally expanding B300 fleet that Telnyx builds and operates end to end. Bring your experience optimizing demanding production workloads to a fleet where you shape the architecture from bare metal to customer endpoint.
  • Own the platform, build the team. A greenfield inference platform where you set the pattern others follow. As a founding member of our China team, you also get a say in who joins next and how the team works.
  • Open-source first. Upstream contribution is part of the job, and conference travel is supported.
  • Based in mainland China, no relocation required. You work remotely with a global, async-friendly team. Should you ever choose to move, we have hiring entities in the Netherlands, the United States, Ireland and Saudi Arabia, and we sponsor visas.

When you apply

Include a brief description of an inference system you personally improved: the bottleneck, your intervention, and the measured result. An anonymized example is welcome.

Board Advisor (Volunteer)

Mothers to Daughters

About Mothers to Daughters:

Mothers to Daughters (M2D) is a 501(c)(3) non-profit dedicated to empowering women across generations through leadership and entrepreneurship training, educational workshops, and networking opportunities. Through intergenerational mentorship and community service, M2D advances gender equality, fosters leadership, and equips women to drive social and economic change in their communities. This handbook outlines our values, policies, and operational procedures to guide team members in fulfilling our mission.

Our Mission at Mothers to Daughters is to accelerate the personal and professional growth of women by connecting them with the lived experiences, authentic insights, and transformative wisdom of successful women. Through intergenerational mentorship, we foster a legacy of economic empowerment, social resilience, and impact-driven innovation, equipping women to lead, innovate, and build sustainable solutions that transcend generations.

Our Vision is a world where women of all generations thrive through the power of intergenerational wisdom, driving inclusivity and gender equity for lasting global impact. By bridging generations, amplifying voices, and breaking down barriers, we aim to create a future where women are elevated to the heights they deserve—leading, innovating, and shaping a more equitable and prosperous world for all.

Our Core Values at Mothers to Daughters are:

  • UnwaveringRespect

    • We honor diverse perspectives and experiences, fostering an environment where every voice is valued.

    • We believe in mutual respect between generations, recognizing the wisdom of experience and the disruptive innovation of youth.

    • We encourage bold yet respectful dialogue in discussions around gender equality, relationships, and personal development.

  • Purpose driven-Trust

    • We prioritize transparency, accountability, and credibility, ensuring that our members, mentors, and sponsors feel confident in our work.

    • We believe trust is the cornerstone of meaningful mentorship, enabling honest, courageous conversations and impactful guidance.

    • We commit to upholding the integrity of our mission, maintaining the highest ethical standards in all our partnerships and programs.

  • Synergistic Collaboration

    • We recognize that transformative change happens when we work together across generations, cultures, and industries.

    • We actively forge alliances with organizations that align with our mission, including men’s groups working toward gender equity.

    • We foster a culture of dynamic knowledge-sharing, ensuring that mentorship is a two-way exchange where both mentors and mentees grow together.

  • Transformational Empathy

    • We understand that each woman’s journey is unique, committing to creating a safe space for shared experiences and personal growth.

    • We recognize societal and personal challenges women face and approach solutions with compassion and pragmatic action.

    • We champion vulnerability as a strength, encouraging open discussions about both breakthroughs and setbacks.

  • Impact-Driven Entrepreneurial Spirit

    • We believe in equipping women with the skills, mindset, and resources to take ownership of their futures—whether through career advancement, leadership, or business ventures.

    • We encourage innovation, agility, and adaptability, ensuring our programs evolve to meet the shifting needs of our global community.

    • We emphasize bold resilience, helping women break barriers, embrace risk, and lead with confidence.

  • Unapologetic Authenticity

    • We embrace and celebrate individuality, encouraging women to bring their whole selves to the table.

    • We champion unapologetic self-expression, ensuring that every woman’s voice is heard, respected, and amplified.

    • We commit to honest, transparent communication, rejecting performative feminism in favor of practical, high-impact actions that drive real change.

  • Future-focused Innovation

    • We embrace bold, transformative thinking, pushing boundaries to create solutions that redefine possibilities for women.

    • We leverage technology, data, and creativity to amplify mentorship, leadership, and economic empowerment initiatives.

    • We foster a culture of continuous learning and reinvention, ensuring that women stay ahead in an ever-evolving global landscape.

Position Overview:

We are seeking a Board Advisor with board governance expertise. The successful candidate will have deep understanding of international development issues, strong analytical skills, proven experience in designing and implementing social impact programs, excellent communication abilities, and a network within the UN system and broader social impact. As part of our dynamic and mission-driven team, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of our organization and advancing our mission.

  • UN experience:

    • Prior work with UN agencies, programs, or funds in a relevant capacity (e.g., policy development, program management, advocacy)

    • Familiarity with UN frameworks, procedures, and decision-making processes

    • Understanding of the UN system's strengths and limitations

  • Social impact expertise:

    • Proven track record in designing and implementing social impact initiatives across diverse areas like poverty alleviation, education, health, climate change adaptation, or gender equality

    • Expertise in developing and measuring social impact metrics

    • Knowledge of best practices in social impact assessment and reporting

  • Strategic thinking:

    • Capacity to develop comprehensive strategic plans aligned with UN goals and organizational priorities

    • Ability to identify emerging trends and potential opportunities in the social impact landscape

    • Skillful at navigating complex political and stakeholder dynamics

  • Communication and advocacy skills:

    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills to effectively present complex issues to diverse audiences

    • Proven ability to advocate for social impact initiatives at various levels, including with policymakers and donors

    • Expertise in building strong relationships with key stakeholders

  • Leadership and collaboration:

    • Ability to lead and facilitate collaborative efforts with diverse teams and stakeholders

    • Strong interpersonal skills to build consensus and foster positive working relationships

Commitment:

Reporting to the SVP of Real Estate and Construction, this executive leader will have enterprise accountability for the strategy, governance and execution of Tailored Brands’ real estate program across all brands and markets. The Sr. Director will lead, coach and develop the Directors responsible for market strategy, site selection, lease negotiations, portfolio optimization and corporate real estate, ensuring consistent standards, disciplined execution and strong financial outcomes. This position will oversee the transactional management and strategic planning for retail stores, corporate offices, HUBs, Distribution Centers and other leased or owned properties. The role will provide senior leadership for relocation, replacement, renewal, expansion, closure, disposition and other real estate initiatives, serving as a key advisor to the SVP of Real Estate and Construction and executive partners across the Company.

What You’ll Do | Key Accountabilities

  • Leads and develops the Directors across the Real Estate organization by establishing clear accountability, priorities, performance expectations and operating rhythms; builds bench strength through coaching, mentoring, succession planning and effective talent management.
  • Establishes portfolio governance, decision criteria, approval processes and key performance indicators to ensure consistent, data-driven recommendations and execution across all real estate functions.
  • Partners with executive and cross-functional teams to identify opportunities, align real estate actions with corporate and brand strategies, and translate business priorities into actionable market and portfolio plans.
  • Oversees analysis of demographics, income levels, customer density, competitive activity, traffic patterns, retail synergies and other market data to determine site feasibility, portfolio opportunities and investment priorities.
  • Directs the development and performance management of the broker and developer network. Establishes company standards for site development and economic terms, ensures the Directors and brokers apply those standards consistently, and monitors results and service quality.
  • Provides senior oversight of lease and transaction negotiations, including rent and lease terms, site conditions, landlord contributions, business points and legal requirements. Serves as an escalation point for complex, high-value or strategically important negotiations in partnership with Real Estate and Legal leaders.
  • Maintains senior relationships with landlords, developers, brokers and strategic partners; represents Tailored Brands in important portfolio discussions and ensures the Company is positioned for future development opportunities.
  • Establishes disciplined pipeline, project management and reporting practices across the organization, ensuring timely escalation of risks, decisions, dependencies and resource needs.
  • Owns the accuracy and credibility of the new-store and real estate initiative pipeline, including 12- to 24-month opening projections, portfolio actions, lease events and other enterprise commitments.
  • Provides executive oversight of reporting for existing-location lease actions, new-store activity, owned assets, corporate properties and other real estate initiatives; uses reporting to drive accountability and continuous improvement.
  • Champions an owner’s mindset, balancing customer and brand needs with long-term portfolio value, risk management, capital discipline and total occupancy economics.
  • Oversees all transactions involving the owned-assets portfolio, including acquisitions, dispositions and sale-leaseback transactions, in coordination with Finance, Legal and other stakeholders.
  • Has strategic oversight of the portfolio of logistics and transportation HUBs, Distribution Centers, Corporate Offices and other corporate-supporting locations, including portfolio planning, lease strategy, capital needs and business continuity considerations.
  • Serves as a senior advisor to the SVP of Real Estate and Construction and executive leadership on enterprise real estate matters and leads other strategic initiatives as assigned.

Skills & Experience

  • Minimum Requirements: Bachelor’s degree required in Business, Real Estate or a related field; 15+ years of relevant experience, including significant experience leading real estate teams and complex, multi-market programs.
  • Preferred Requirements: Master’s degree in Business, Real Estate or a related field; 7+ years of people-leadership experience and a demonstrated track record overseeing retail real estate site selection, lease negotiations, portfolio strategy and high-volume transaction execution (20+ annual new deals at the team level).
  • Executive-level verbal and written communication skills; highly organized, detail-oriented and proficient in Microsoft Office and presentation tools.
  • Strong financial acumen, including the ability to interpret P&L statements, evaluate investment returns and occupancy economics, and guide the development of effective action plans tied to strategic objectives.
  • Knowledge of demographic mapping, market planning and real estate analytics tools required.
  • Exceptional people-leadership skills with the ability to attract, develop, coach and retain high-performing Directors and broader real estate teams.
  • Strong negotiation, influence and executive presence, with the ability to build alignment and make sound decisions at all levels of the organization and with external partners.
  • Deep understanding of complex leases, transaction structures, corresponding legal terms and real estate risk management.
  • Proficient in financial analysis, spreadsheets, presentations, portfolio reporting, pipeline management and enterprise program management.
  • Strategic thinker who can manage multiple priorities, make decisions with incomplete information, create operating discipline and drive accountability across a distributed organization.
Please note that you do not need to qualify for all requirements to be considered. We encourage you to apply if you can meet most of the requirements and are comfortable opening a dialog to be considered.

Work Environment, Physical & Mental Demands

  • Ability to sit and work at a computer keyboard for extended periods of time
  • Ability to stoop, kneel, bend at the waist, and reach daily
  • Able to lift and move up to 25 pounds occasionally
  • Must utilize visual acuity, speech and hearing, hand and eye coordination and manual dexterity necessary to operate a computer and office equipment
  • Hours regularly 40 hours per week, as work dictates, from remote location
  • Must be based on the East Coast or West Coast, near a major metropolitan airport.
  • A minimum of 25% travel is required, including market trips, industry conventions and other events, landlord and developer portfolio meetings, team meetings and other travel as designated by the SVP of Real Estate and Construction.

Benefits

This role is eligible for health, dental and vision insurance, prescription drug, retirement savings (401k, employer-funded retirement plans, deferred compensation, and other defined-benefit or defined-contribution), life insurance, accident and disability, paid time off for sick leave, vacation, bereavement, jury duty, holidays (9 days per year), wellbeing program, commuter, adoption assistance, legal services, and employee merchandise discounts.

Work-Life Balance

We understand the demands of work, school, family, and personal responsibilities. Through our work-life resources and programs we offer services for every stage of life to help you manage the day-to-day needs. We offer programs such as:
  • Meeting-Free Fridays (encouraged) | so you can catch up on work and self-development
  • Summer Fridays | from Memorial Day to Labor Day so you can enjoy a head-start to the weekend
  • Holiday Early Departure | close out early the business day before a company observed holiday

Other compensation may include a 25% Annual Incentive Plan (AIP) bonus paid out according to policy. Base pay information is based on market location and may be subject to prevailing wage laws, if applicable.

About Anovium

Anovium is a technology consultancy that transforms operations through intelligent innovation. We specialize in helping logistics, transportation, and distribution companies modernize their operations while building foundations for future growth. By combining deep industry expertise with technical innovation, we deliver practical solutions that drive measurable business outcomes.

» Our Approach

We believe in the power of practical innovation. We focus on real results - helping traditional industries embrace modern technology without disrupting what makes them successful. Our approach is rooted in understanding your business first, then applying technology to solve real challenges.

» Our Culture

At Anovium, we're building a team of experts who understand both technology and industry. We value:
- Deep expertise paired with continuous learning
- Practical innovation over theoretical possibilities
- Long-term partnerships built on measurable results
- Balance of technical excellence and human understanding

» Who We're Looking For

We seek professionals who combine technical expertise with industry understanding. The ideal Anovium team member:
- Thrives on transforming complex business challenges into elegant solutions
- Values both technical excellence and practical business outcomes
- Brings a partnership mentality to client relationships
- Has a genuine interest in logistics, transportation, or healthcare technology
- Embraces our philosophy of sophisticated innovation with practical impact
Our team members don't just implement technology – they help traditional industries embrace the future while understanding their foundations. If you're excited about bringing meaningful technological transformation to established industries, we want to talk to you.

Full Stack Product Engineer

TL/DR: You're responsible for building amazing ships. You're a wizard at your craft, while also being a team player that can guide the team to successful deliveries.

The Opportunity

We are looking for strong developers to augment our growing team and maintain our high standards of quality in delivery.
Examples of projects you might work on include: med tech solutions, digital consumer aid products, legal tech products, productivity solutions, web3, etc.

What You'll Do

  • Ship Value Fast. You’ll move fast, constantly shipping value consisting of clean, empathetic, efficient code. Bugs happen - own them; fix them.
  • Contribute Broadly. You’ll work with and contribute to product, design, engineering and architecture, applying your skills and insights to plan, develop, and own new tasks.
  • Own the Process. You’ll own responsibility for your delivery and execution. You’ll forge new paths forward while not waiting to be handheld.
  • Improve and Grow. You’ll be learning, improving, and teaching alongside others who love to do the same. You’ll lead and give constructive feedback. You’ll challenge both yourself and your team as they challenge you.
  • Make an Impact. You’ll be working with small teams. The things you do will have a large impact on shaping the delivery of products and features.

Who You Are

  • You love to build and deliver. You’re obsessed with creation and delivery of value.
  • You are a wizard. You have end-to-end experience building out web and/or mobile applications. Others look up to and respect your technical skill sets. Your past experiences will help guide you and your team through challenges.
  • You thrive in fast-paced environments. This is an environment of high iteration. There is constant change and sometimes little guidance. You aren’t held back by the fear of being wrong or making a mistake.
  • You are empathetic for developers and consumers. You build with future and current developers in mind – making it easy for others (or even yourself!) to pick up where you left off. You also build with your consumer in mind.
  • You diagnose problems. You challenge prevailing assumptions and dig to the root of issues. You solve problems rather than treat symptoms.
  • You’re a strong leader. You’re passionate. You take pride in your craftsmanship and are passionate about quality software engineering.
  • You are candid. You’re candid, but respectful. You share pertinent information, even when difficult. You admit mistakes. You openly disagree and explain why.

What You Have

  • Experiences:
  • 4+ years of building and shipping production-quality software systems
  • Backend technologies like Node.js, C#/.Net, Go, or Java/Spring
  • Frontend technologies like React.js or Vue.js
  • TypeScript
  • Building human-centered user experiences
  • Working cross-functionally with managers, designers, and engineers
  • Creating self documenting, modular, testable, performant code.
  • Deep understanding of the whole engineering stack, from database, servers, to UI

    • (Bonus)

  • Experience with React Native, GraphQL, DevOps, or CI/CD.
  • Knowledgeable in web3.

Ecosystems You May Work In

  • Different projects have a different combination of the following:
  • General. JavaScript (specifically, we favor TypeScript)
  • Front End. React.js, Vue.js
  • Back End. Node.js, Go, C#/.Net, Java/Spring
  • Mobile. React Native
  • Desktop. Electron
  • DB. MySQL, MongoDB
  • API. REST, GraphQL
  • Other. Python, LookML, Docker & more

DevOps Staff Platform Engineer

Location: Remote (Canada)

Compensation: $135,000 - $170,000 CAD + bonus + meaningful equity

About Orion Digital

Orion Digital Corp (NASDAQ/TSX: ORIO) is a publicly listed Canadian fintech operating a multi-engine financial platform spanning lending (Mogo), payments (Carta), and wealth (Intelligent Investing).

We have moved past the traditional fintech model. Capital allocation, decisioning, and risk management sit at the core of how the business creates value, and AI runs as an enabling layer across the platform rather than as a standalone product narrative. That layer is real and in use, and the work now is making it faster, safer, and harder to break.

Why this role exists

This role builds that layer.

Platform engineering here is not a support function. Multiple business lines, regulated entities, and a public company's reporting obligations all run on infrastructure this team owns. Every deployment path, permission boundary, and audit trail either makes faster decisioning possible or quietly caps how fast the business can move.

Which means the platform is where the strategy succeeds or stalls. If deploying takes a day, if an agent cannot safely touch production, if nobody can tell what changed and why, the enabling layer stays theoretical. We are hiring a Staff Platform Engineer to build it properly.

The shift we are hiring for

Most platform teams build for human developers. Ours builds for humans and agents, across multiple business lines and regulated entities. That changes the job:

  • Golden paths become machine-executable contracts, not wiki pages. An agent has to be able to discover them, invoke them, and verify the result.
  • Every probabilistic step needs a deterministic gate behind it. Tests, policy checks, and schema validation stop being hygiene and become the control system that lets autonomy scale safely.
  • Agents are identities. They need scoped credentials, bounded blast radius, and audit trails that hold up across lending, payments, and securities regulation.
  • Observability has to answer a new question. Not just "is the service healthy" but "did the agent do the right thing, and how do we know."

If that is already how you think about the problem, keep reading.

What you will do

Build the substrate for agentic engineering

  • Design and run the execution environments agents work in: sandboxed, reproducible, permissioned, disposable.
  • Stand up and own our MCP and tool-gateway layer so agents reach infrastructure through governed interfaces instead of ad hoc credentials.
  • Turn CI/CD into a validation loop: fast deterministic gates an agent can retry against until it passes, with humans on the loop rather than in it.

Own the platform

  • Multi-cloud Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, and GitOps (ArgoCD) delivery. Hands on keyboard, not diagrams.
  • Drive infrastructure modernization across our cloud environments, including the unglamorous parts: dependency mapping, and documentation that survives your absence.
  • Serve every product line without building a separate platform for each one. Where they genuinely differ, respect it. Where they have drifted for no reason, converge them.
  • Treat security and compliance as design constraints from the first commit rather than a review at the end.

Take toil off the company

  • Push autonomous remediation into the paths that page people today. The target is alerts that resolve themselves and incidents where the first responder is an agent arriving with a hypothesis already tested.
  • Own the numbers: deploy frequency, lead time, change failure rate, MTTR, and the share of operational work running without a human in the middle. Move them quarter over quarter.
  • Work outside engineering too. Operations, compliance, and support are full of repetitive work a well-built platform can absorb.

What you need

Non-negotiable

  • Deep, current production experience with Kubernetes, Terraform, and a modern GitOps deployment stack. You have owned what you built, including running it in production rather than handing it off once it shipped.
  • Real cloud depth. We run across AWS and OCI, so experience in both is an advantage, but what matters is genuine production depth in at least one and the appetite to get fluent in the other quickly.
  • You run coding and ops agents as part of your daily work, and you can show us. Sustained real use on real systems (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or equivalent, plus whatever you have wired together yourself), not a trial and an opinion. Be ready to walk through something you shipped this month where an agent did most of the typing and you did the judging.
  • Strong opinions about where autonomy belongs and where it does not, informed by having been burned at least once.
  • Writing clear enough to be read by a junior engineer and a model.

Advantage

  • You have built internal developer platforms, MCP servers, or agent tooling that other engineers actually adopted.
  • Non-human identity, secrets architecture, or policy-as-code in a regulated environment.
  • Re-platforming at scale, especially where the old system could not go down.
  • Opinions about how to evaluate infrastructure agents. Almost nobody has these yet.

We are not screening on years of experience as a proxy for capability. We will look at what you have built and how fast you build.

How we work

  • Small teams, high ownership, short distance between decision and deployment.
  • We would rather collaborate than dictate, and we know when to do it well versus when to do it quickly.
  • Output is the measure.

E-commerce Operations & Data Analyst – Remote

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Business Hours

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring an E-commerce Operations & Data Analyst to support the day-to-day logistics, inventory management, operational reporting, and data analysis of a growing e-commerce business.

This is an operations-first role, not a highly technical data engineering position. You’ll coordinate freight and inventory, maintain accurate operational data, manage Shopify information, build reports and dashboards, and use spreadsheets to help the business make better operational decisions.

You’ll also use modern AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude to streamline repetitive work, improve reporting, and make internal processes more efficient.

The ideal candidate combines logistics and e-commerce experience with strong spreadsheet and analytical skills and enjoys continuously improving how operations are run.

What You’ll Own

Logistics & Freight Coordination

  • Manage freight and shipment coordination from start to finish.
  • Track shipments, deliveries, and fulfillment timelines.
  • Coordinate closely with warehouses and logistics partners.
  • Maintain visibility into shipment status and proactively address delays.
  • Keep accurate and organized logistics records.
  • Ensure day-to-day logistics workflows run smoothly.

Inventory & Purchase Order Management

  • Monitor inventory levels and stock availability.
  • Create and manage purchase orders based on inventory needs.
  • Use sales trends and forecasting data to support purchasing decisions.
  • Help prevent stockouts and unnecessary overstock.
  • Maintain accurate inventory trackers and records.
  • Support inventory planning across products and fulfillment channels.

E-commerce Operations

  • Manage and update product and operational data within Shopify.
  • Maintain accurate product information and internal records.
  • Support day-to-day e-commerce operational workflows.
  • Coordinate information across inventory, logistics, sales, and customer operations.
  • Identify operational issues and help resolve them before they impact customers.

Reporting & Data Analysis

  • Maintain structured operational spreadsheets and trackers.
  • Generate recurring reports covering:
    • Sales
    • Inventory
    • Returns
    • Customer service
    • Product performance
    • Logistics
  • Analyze operational data to identify trends, issues, and opportunities.
  • Build and maintain dashboards that give leadership clear visibility into performance.
  • Support inventory forecasting and operational planning using reliable data.

AI & Workflow Improvement

  • Use ChatGPT, Claude, and similar AI tools to improve day-to-day operational workflows.
  • Identify repetitive processes that can be simplified or automated.

DevOps Staff Platform Engineer

Location: Remote (Canada)

Compensation: $135,000 - $170,000 CAD + bonus + meaningful equity

About Orion Digital

Orion Digital Corp (NASDAQ/TSX: ORIO) is a publicly listed Canadian fintech operating a multi-engine financial platform spanning lending (Mogo), payments (Carta), and wealth (Intelligent Investing).

We have moved past the traditional fintech model. Capital allocation, decisioning, and risk management sit at the core of how the business creates value, and AI runs as an enabling layer across the platform rather than as a standalone product narrative. That layer is real and in use, and the work now is making it faster, safer, and harder to break.

Why this role exists

This role builds that layer.

Platform engineering here is not a support function. Multiple business lines, regulated entities, and a public company's reporting obligations all run on infrastructure this team owns. Every deployment path, permission boundary, and audit trail either makes faster decisioning possible or quietly caps how fast the business can move.

Which means the platform is where the strategy succeeds or stalls. If deploying takes a day, if an agent cannot safely touch production, if nobody can tell what changed and why, the enabling layer stays theoretical. We are hiring a Staff Platform Engineer to build it properly.

The shift we are hiring for

Most platform teams build for human developers. Ours builds for humans and agents, across multiple business lines and regulated entities. That changes the job:

  • Golden paths become machine-executable contracts, not wiki pages. An agent has to be able to discover them, invoke them, and verify the result.
  • Every probabilistic step needs a deterministic gate behind it. Tests, policy checks, and schema validation stop being hygiene and become the control system that lets autonomy scale safely.
  • Agents are identities. They need scoped credentials, bounded blast radius, and audit trails that hold up across lending, payments, and securities regulation.
  • Observability has to answer a new question. Not just "is the service healthy" but "did the agent do the right thing, and how do we know."

If that is already how you think about the problem, keep reading.

What you will do

Build the substrate for agentic engineering

  • Design and run the execution environments agents work in: sandboxed, reproducible, permissioned, disposable.
  • Stand up and own our MCP and tool-gateway layer so agents reach infrastructure through governed interfaces instead of ad hoc credentials.
  • Turn CI/CD into a validation loop: fast deterministic gates an agent can retry against until it passes, with humans on the loop rather than in it.

Own the platform

  • Multi-cloud Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, and GitOps (ArgoCD) delivery. Hands on keyboard, not diagrams.
  • Drive infrastructure modernization across our cloud environments, including the unglamorous parts: dependency mapping, and documentation that survives your absence.
  • Serve every product line without building a separate platform for each one. Where they genuinely differ, respect it. Where they have drifted for no reason, converge them.
  • Treat security and compliance as design constraints from the first commit rather than a review at the end.

Take toil off the company

  • Push autonomous remediation into the paths that page people today. The target is alerts that resolve themselves and incidents where the first responder is an agent arriving with a hypothesis already tested.
  • Own the numbers: deploy frequency, lead time, change failure rate, MTTR, and the share of operational work running without a human in the middle. Move them quarter over quarter.
  • Work outside engineering too. Operations, compliance, and support are full of repetitive work a well-built platform can absorb.

What you need

Non-negotiable

  • Deep, current production experience with Kubernetes, Terraform, and a modern GitOps deployment stack. You have owned what you built, including running it in production rather than handing it off once it shipped.
  • Real cloud depth. We run across AWS and OCI, so experience in both is an advantage, but what matters is genuine production depth in at least one and the appetite to get fluent in the other quickly.
  • You run coding and ops agents as part of your daily work, and you can show us. Sustained real use on real systems (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or equivalent, plus whatever you have wired together yourself), not a trial and an opinion. Be ready to walk through something you shipped this month where an agent did most of the typing and you did the judging.
  • Strong opinions about where autonomy belongs and where it does not, informed by having been burned at least once.
  • Writing clear enough to be read by a junior engineer and a model.

Advantage

  • You have built internal developer platforms, MCP servers, or agent tooling that other engineers actually adopted.
  • Non-human identity, secrets architecture, or policy-as-code in a regulated environment.
  • Re-platforming at scale, especially where the old system could not go down.
  • Opinions about how to evaluate infrastructure agents. Almost nobody has these yet.

We are not screening on years of experience as a proxy for capability. We will look at what you have built and how fast you build.

How we work

  • Small teams, high ownership, short distance between decision and deployment.
  • We would rather collaborate than dictate, and we know when to do it well versus when to do it quickly.
  • Output is the measure.

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring an E-commerce Operations & Data Analyst to support the day-to-day logistics, inventory management, operational reporting, and data analysis of a growing e-commerce business.

This is an operations-first role, not a highly technical data engineering position. You’ll coordinate freight and inventory, maintain accurate operational data, manage Shopify information, build reports and dashboards, and use spreadsheets to help the business make better operational decisions.

You’ll also use modern AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude to streamline repetitive work, improve reporting, and make internal processes more efficient.

The ideal candidate combines logistics and e-commerce experience with strong spreadsheet and analytical skills and enjoys continuously improving how operations are run.

What You’ll Own

Logistics & Freight Coordination

  • Manage freight and shipment coordination from start to finish.
  • Track shipments, deliveries, and fulfillment timelines.
  • Coordinate closely with warehouses and logistics partners.
  • Maintain visibility into shipment status and proactively address delays.
  • Keep accurate and organized logistics records.
  • Ensure day-to-day logistics workflows run smoothly.

Inventory & Purchase Order Management

  • Monitor inventory levels and stock availability.
  • Create and manage purchase orders based on inventory needs.
  • Use sales trends and forecasting data to support purchasing decisions.
  • Help prevent stockouts and unnecessary overstock.
  • Maintain accurate inventory trackers and records.
  • Support inventory planning across products and fulfillment channels.

E-commerce Operations

  • Manage and update product and operational data within Shopify.
  • Maintain accurate product information and internal records.
  • Support day-to-day e-commerce operational workflows.
  • Coordinate information across inventory, logistics, sales, and customer operations.
  • Identify operational issues and help resolve them before they impact customers.

Reporting & Data Analysis

  • Maintain structured operational spreadsheets and trackers.
  • Generate recurring reports covering:
    • Sales
    • Inventory
    • Returns
    • Customer service
    • Product performance
    • Logistics
  • Analyze operational data to identify trends, issues, and opportunities.
  • Build and maintain dashboards that give leadership clear visibility into performance.
