raw.description:
Director of Product Management, Agentic Platform Enablement Experience (APEX)

Remote - US

Overview:

Pax8 is the global AI and cloud Marketplace for small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs). Pax8 connects service providers and technology companies on a unified platform to discover, buy, sell, deploy and manage technology solutions for SMBs. More than 47,000 IT partners and 800,000 SMBs rely on Pax8 for expertise, automation and real-time insights to stay productive, protected and prepared for the AI economy. Learn more at pax8.com.

Position Summary:

Join Pax8 as Director of Product Management for Agentic Platform Enablement Experience (APEX), the most technical product leader on the APEX team and the day-to-day owner of our agentic platform surfaces, including agent SDKs, tool use and orchestration, the internal developer platform and the autonomy and trust experience that makes agentic capability safe to adopt. You’ll be working with leadership and teams to build and deliver a product with capabilities that has no established precedent. Reporting to the VP of Product Management for APEX, you are the second seat in the practice and the one closest to the code.

This is a principal-caliber individual contributor role with people leadership attached: you set product strategy and launch bars for non-deterministic systems yourself, you stay hands-on in product and engineering repos, and you manage, coach and grow a team of product managers doing the same work.

Essential Responsibilities (includes, but is not limited to):

  • Own end-to-end product strategy, roadmap, and launch criteria for the APEX platform surfaces (agent SDK, tool use and orchestration, developer platform, autonomy and trust UX) across a 1-6 quarter horizon; contribute to the portfolio strategy above it
  • Set and own launch-readiness criteria for non-deterministic systems in partnership with Engineering, Security, Research, and Design; make the ship vs hold call yourself
  • Define the autonomy spectrum per capability (human-in-the-loop, AI-assisted, agentic) and the trust and control experience that makes it legible to the people using it
  • Identify and mitigate misuse and risk pre-launch; define the monitoring, audit trail, and rollback that ships with every autonomous capability
  • Personally build prototypes, scripts, and evaluation harnesses to test product decisions, working inside engineering and product repos and internal SDKs as a peer user
  • Be a daily, hands-on user of the platform you own; file precise, implementable bug reports and behavior-change requests
  • Instrument adoption, quality, and safety metrics from day one; run experiments and A/B tests to prove impact rather than assert it
  • Manage, coach, and develop a team of product managers; own development plans and performance conversations for each PM, and raise the craft bar for technical, data-driven product judgment on agentic systems
  • Hire and develop AI-fluent, technically credible product managers; partner with your leader on staffing plans, resourcing needs, and headcount justification
  • Translate vision and portfolio strategy into sequenced, actionable roadmaps tied to business OKRs; own domain-level OKRs and report clearly on progress, risk, and trade-offs
  • Make build/buy/partner decisions for capabilities within APEX, with explicit ROI reasoning
  • Build trusted relationships with peers in Engineering, Design, Data, Security, Marketing, and GTM; secure cross-functional alignment on the APEX strategy and keep it coherent with adjacent domains
  • Ensure responsible AI, ethics, compliance, and legal reviews are completed for products in your domain, following company standards
  • Represent the platform internally and externally: enablement, developer relations, launch communications, and public launches that build credibility for Pax8 in the agentic space
  • Use AI tools and agents in daily work, and model that practice for the team

Skills & Experience:

Core Skills & Experience:

  • At least eight to ten (8 – 10) years of experience in product management or an equivalent role
  • At least three (3) years of experience leading product managers, including experience growing a team
  • Engineering background required: prior professional experience as a software engineer, or an equivalent track record driving technical product direction; comfortable writing code personally at prototype quality (prototypes, scripts, eval harnesses) without handing it to an engineer first
  • Track record delivering product capabilities on a developer-focused platform (APIs, SDKs, CLIs, developer tools), backed by pointable evidence: launch posts, press coverage, changelogs, or documentation you shipped
  • Track record of leading multiple products that drive measurable outcomes, and of leading a significant product, platform, automation, or process transformation
  • Data-driven by nature: designs and runs experiments, instruments adoption and quality metrics from day one, and can show a record of moving them, not just launching features
  • Scrupulous about value for Pax8 and our partners; able to articulate and defend expected ROI
  • Excellent communication, organizational, and people skills; can present a clear narrative to senior leadership
  • Comfortable with ambiguity; adapts quickly and keeps the team oriented when priorities shift

Agentic Platform Depth:

  • Deep, firsthand fluency with how frontier models and agentic systems behave - tool use, planning, multi-step execution, and common failure modes - and with the current agentic platform landscape (agent SDKs, computer-use interfaces, orchestration frameworks)
  • Able to read model evals and capability reports directly and translate them into launch bars, acceptance criteria, and roadmap decisions
  • Sets safety, authority, and escalation boundaries for autonomous capability, and can defend those boundaries to engineering, security, and executive audiences
  • Reached via Breadth (coherence across several interdependent, complex product areas) or Depth (sole expert in one hard, fast-moving product problem) - same level, either route

AI Skills & Experience:

  • Daily experience with tools like Claude, Microsoft Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Atlassian AI, Figma (design collaboration and AI product research), Pendo (AI product analytics and research collaboration) - with a working view of where each fits in the product workflow
  • Solid understanding of AI capabilities and limitations, including cost, latency, and quality trade-offs
  • Use enterprise-approved AI tools for daily productivity, and redirect the team away from unapproved tools
  • Apply data classification and privacy principles when using AI, and hold the team to the same
  • Practice responsible AI: recognize bias, fairness, and transparency requirements and build them into acceptance criteria
  • Effective prompting and context-setting - clear instructions, context, iterative refinement - and share what works across the team
  • Own the responsible AI ethics review for customer-facing AI products within your domain
  • Measure AI product outcomes: accuracy, user satisfaction, adoption, and business impact
  • Own and apply the company AI standard within your domain: human-in-the-loop, AI-assisted, and agentic decisions are deliberate, documented, and consistently applied
  • AI Proficiency Expectation: Expert

Preferred Skills:

  • Multiple years of professional experience as a software engineer prior to moving into product, beyond the minimum engineering background required above
  • Has personally built agentic evaluations (SWE-bench-style suites, LLM-judge rubrics, model-behavior regression harnesses), not just commissioned them
  • Direct experience with research and design teams as a daily collaborator, not a periodic stakeholder
  • Took a research result or internal prototype into a production product used at scale
  • Defined a new product category or UX pattern with no established precedent (early agentic UX, autonomous coding tools, computer-use interfaces)
  • External visibility in the agentic product space: talks, published product thinking, recognized contribution to industry framing of autonomy, trust, or agent UX

What Success Looks Like:

  • The APEX product vision and strategy are clearly communicated and visibly aligned to business outcomes.
  • Agentic capabilities ship with explicit authority, safety, and escalation boundaries, and with the monitoring, audit trail, and rollback that make them operable.
  • Launch bars for non-deterministic systems are defined, applied consistently, and trusted by Engineering, Security, and executive leadership.
  • Adoption, quality, and safety metrics exist from day one and show measurable movement.
  • Build/buy/partner decisions within the domain are grounded in measurable value.
  • The product management team is AI-fluent, technically credible, well-coached, and growing against clear development plans - with at least one PM ready for the next level.
  • Engineering, Design, Data, Security, and senior stakeholders have clarity on priorities, trade-offs, and delivery expectations.
  • Escalations to your leader are the exception, and they arrive with a recommendation attached.

Required Behaviors:

Compassionate Candour - We aim to assist others with candid, actionable feedback.

Seek to Understand - Be open, curious and committed to learning.

At Niagara, we’re looking for Team Members who want to be part of achieving our mission to provide our customers the highest quality most affordable bottled water.

Consider applying here, if you want to:

  • Work in an entrepreneurial and dynamic environment with a chance to make an impact.
  • Develop lasting relationships with great people.
  • Have the opportunity to build a satisfying career.

We offer competitive compensation and benefits packages for our Team Members.

Geologist (Remote, Up to 75% travel)

This Geologist ensures the delivery of high-quality spring water collected in compliance with FDA/IBWA requirements and maintains up-to-date and readily accessible information on Niagara-utilized spring sources. The role will manage the evaluation and qualification of new spring and water well sources for expansion plants and as back up sources for existing facilities.

This position reports to the Principal Geologist.

Detailed Description - The Geologist shall do, or supervise the Geologist I and II positions in doing, the following:

Technical Management and Monitoring of Niagara-Utilized Spring Sources.

  • Be the primary point of contact for, and liaison to spring source owners fostering professional working relationships

  • Maintain routine contact with all spring owners.

  • Conduct as-needed, spring source audits to ensure compliance with Niagara operating requirements

  • Monitor overall spring source water quality and any changes or trends over time

  • Track spring source permits, expirations and renewals

  • Develop and maintain database/documentation supporting spring SOI, hydrogeology, engineering and permits

  • Be a technical resource to spring owners as they upgrade or modify their facilities

  • Track regulatory changes pertaining to spring sources

  • Maintain awareness of land use activities and potential contaminant threats in the vicinity of the spring sources

  • Be the Niagara representative at regulatory and local community meetings (when necessary)

  • Partner in spring improvement work under a cost-recovery agreement with the spring owner where appropriate an in conjunction with the Procurement team

Evaluate New Spring Water Sources for Expansion Projects and Ongoing Operations.

  • Work with the Procurement and Expansion teams to identify spring sources in the vicinity of proposed Expansion facilities

  • Evaluate the technical merits and viability of prospect spring sources

  • Assist with spring site development layout/design

  • Prepare planning cost estimates for improvements that may be necessary to bring prospect springs online

  • Provide technical support to Niagara's Contracts Team

  • Seek/develop opportunities for Niagara-owned spring sources

Spring Source Information System

  • Work with staff to build database information on each spring source

  • Maintain the water quality data base and provide statistics and graphing trends for spring sources when needed

Technical Management of Niagara-Owned Groundwater Water Supply Wells

  • Water well siting, design, permitting, drilling and installation; testing and maintenance

  • Aquifer testing and water quality sampling

  • Documentation and report preparation

Customer Support

  • Provide information to Niagara's Consumer Affairs Team to assist them in answering customer questions

  • Meet with customers and make presentations as necessary to assure them of Niagara's spring source quality and integrity

raw.description:
LOCATION:Remote – must live in or near Vaya’s Western NC region. Incumbent in this role must maintain residency in North Carolina or within 40 miles from the NC border. This is a home-based position that requires community travel.

GENERAL STATEMENT OF JOB

The Transitions to Community Living (TCL) Community Liaison’s primary objectives are to provide education to members/recipients and entities stakeholders about TCL, educating providers on how to identify and report barriers, aid in eliminating barriers, provide and create training opportunities and how to access TCL and via the RSVP (Referral Screening Verification Program) process. This position works with various community stakeholders such as the individual, family, LRPs, community/state hospitals, providers, shelters, and adult care homes. This position will work closely and collaboratively with members of the TCL Team in order to meet the established time frames with requests for required documentation as needed through the process. This position ensures that the specific functions related to the Department of Justice and RSVP are followed. This is a mobile position that will require working in various locations throughout and beyond Vaya Health’s catchment area.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

Community Education/Liaison Responsibilities:

A high level of diplomacy and discretion is required to effectively create buy in, negotiate, and resolve concerns or issues, this requires exceptional interpersonal skills, highly effective communication ability, and the propensity to make prompt independent decisions based upon relevant facts. Problem solving, and conflict resolution skills are essential. Demonstrated effective leadership presence is required, with demonstrated confidence in dealing with unknown and complex issues. Awareness of and sensitivity to the complexities of stakeholder and participant concerns.

  • Educate individuals members/recipients and referral entities (hospitals, providers, FCH, ACH, ALF and other key stakeholders) about the TCL eligibility requirements and the RSVP process.
  • Educate and provide training opportunities to internal and external stakeholders regarding TCL program process and how to identify and report barriers.
  • Cascade information to applicable departments within Vaya Health (Vaya) to assist with eliminating TCL barriers
  • Coordinates with referral entities to address and assess the needs of the members/recipients, educate on appropriate services and levels of care as needed.
  • Identifies gaps in services and intervenes to ensure that the individual receives appropriate care, can refer to MHSU Care Management, if appropriate.
  • Ensures that services for the individual are identified and coordinated across the LME/MCO’s system and with other systems, including primary care.
  • Provides education and assistance in collaboration with local hospitals (and other stakeholders) as appropriate to RSVP.
  • While providing outreach and education in the community, the Liaison may also provide potential members/recipients with information on TCL process.
  • Educate facilities stakeholders when members/recipients do not meet TCL eligibility and provide additional community resources when inquiries are received.
  • Other specific functions as they relate to Diversion, In-Reach, Transition Process and Post-Transition responsibilities as indicated from DMA/DMH.
  • Performs related tasks as required.

Collaboration:

  • Collaborates with other members of TCL team and the community to identify areas of need and provides outreach and education in these areas.
  • Serves as a collaborative partner in identifying system barriers. Attends monthly Vaya Local Barriers Committee as a “voting” member to discuss, collaborate and resolve TCL barriers.
  • Sets up, manages, and facilitates meetings with community stakeholders as appropriate to TCL and RSVP process.
  • Facilitates and coordinates the quarterly ACT/CST Collaborative Meeting with assistance across Vaya departments including Quality Management and Provider Network
  • The TCL Community Liaison will work with consumers members/recipients and providers in multiple communities both within and outside the Vaya catchment
  • Works in partnership with other LME/MCO departments to address identified needs within the catchment area.
  • Collects data from concerning TCL via staff report of concerns and collaborates within teams to find resolution of needs.

Documentation:

The TCL Community Liaison is responsible for documenting in an accurate manner that is clear and concise. This documentation will serve to inform the local organization, state, and federal government. All contacts and interventions with members/recipients will be documented in the consumer’s administrative health record if related to a specific individual need. The TCL Community Liaison is anticipated to support Vaya in meeting monthly reporting requirements required by the Department of Justice Settlement.

Other duties as assigned:

Work is performed with considerable independence, with most work performed in the community and away from the office. Employee is familiar with values and goals of TCL and Care Management and minimal daily instruction is required. Formal supervision is scheduled monthly on an ongoing basis and informal supervision occurs as needed.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, & ABILITIES

  • Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Thorough knowledge of TCL requirements, waiver and contractual requirements, and knowledge of the TCLD database.
  • Knowledge and understanding of the Diagnostic and Statistical manual of Mental Disorders (current version).
  • Considerable knowledge of the MHSU/IDD service array provided through the network of the LME/MCO’s providers.
  • Knowledge of Medicaid eligibility determinations.
  • Ability to independently identify, implement and assess system and organizational priorities relative to TCL Initiatives.
  • Ability to be responsive to team members, internal LME/MCO staff, members/recipients, families, and external partners; communicate clearly and concisely through both verbal and writing skills and case formulation.
  • Ability to make prompt independent decisions based upon relevant facts and established processes.
  • Skill in problem solving, negotiation and conflict resolution to balance the needs of both internal and external customers.
  • High level of diplomacy and discretion is required to effectively negotiate and resolve issues with menial assistance.
  • Ability to independently organize multiple tasks and priorities and to effectively manage and assigned caseload under the pressure of deadlines.
  • Skill in Microsoft Office products (such as Word, Excel, Outlook, Forms, etc.) and Vaya Information Systems is required.

A high level of diplomacy and discretion is required to effectively negotiate and resolve issues with minimal assistance. This will require exceptional interpersonal skills, highly effective communication ability, and the propensity to make prompt independent decisions based upon relevant facts. Problem solving, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills are essential to balance the needs of both internal and external stakeholders. Must be highly skilled at shifting between macro and micro level planning, maintaining both the big picture and seeing that the details are covered.

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

  • A minimum of a Bachelor’s degree from an appropriately accredited university or college in public service administration, psychology, sociology, or social work or a human service programmatic field, preferably with coursework in human service planning and four years of experience in directly related human services program;

OR

  • Graduation from a four-year college or university and four years of administrative or consultative experience in a human service program;

OR

  • A Master’s degree from an appropriately accredited university or college in a related human services field and two years of supervised clinical experience;

Or equivalent combination of education and/or experience.

*Direct related experience is defined a human services experience in the areas of case management, assessment and referral, supportive counseling, intervention, psycho-social therapy, and treatment planning.

AND in addition to one of the above qualifications being met, incumbent:

  • Should have experience working with children, adolescent, and adults with MHSU and IDD diagnoses.
  • Must have an operational knowledge of funding sources and access to existing funds or ability to develop (if needed) or present specialized funding requests.

MENTAL/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Close visual acuity to perform activities such as preparation and analysis of documents; viewing a computer terminal; and extensive reading.
  • Physical activity in this position includes crouching, reaching, walking, talking, hearing and repetitive motion of hands, wrists and fingers.
  • Sedentary work with lifting requirements up to 10 pounds, sitting for extended periods of time.
  • Mental concentration is required in all aspects of work.

RESIDENCY REQUIREMENT: The person in this position is required to reside in North Carolina or within 40 miles of the North Carolina border

SALARY:Depending on qualifications & experience of candidate. This position is exempt and is not eligible for overtime compensation.

DEADLINE FOR APPLICATION:Open Until Filled

APPLY:Vaya Health accepts online applications in our Career Center, please visit.

Vaya Health is an equal opportunity employer.

Our Purpose

At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne, your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.

About Us

SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.

Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

What Are We Looking For?

We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.

As an Account Executive, SMB at SentinelOne, you own the full sales cycle into organizations of 51 to 500 employees. You bring relevant sales experience and a track record in cybersecurity or SaaS, and you have closed significant deals and exceeded revenue targets before. In this role you build strong proficiency in SMB territory management and sales. Navigating the partner community is essential, and your deepening understanding of cybersecurity, deal structure, customer management, and territory specifics becomes a real asset.

This role covers a West Coast territory, including metro areas such as Los Angelos and San Diego.

What Will You Do?

Primary responsibilities include:

  • Drive revenue across your territory through a mix of outbound prospecting, and partner-sourced opportunities.
  • Own the full sales cycle: prospecting, discovery, demonstration, negotiation, and close.
  • Create, maintain, and execute a territory plan, and learn to scale your coverage through the channel.
  • Work with channel managers, resellers, and the field sales team on joint go-to-market plans that accelerate new logo acquisition.
  • Prepare for every engagement, internal and external, and organize your effort around hitting and exceeding quota.
  • Forecast to within 10% of your initial call, deliver an accurate weekly commit, and break key deals out in Clari by quarter and month. No hidden deals.
  • Present the SentinelOne sales deck with confidence, and structure calls around what you heard, the problem you are solving, MEDDPICC, and the proposed solution.
  • Prepare, lead, and present to C-Level buyers and below, and pull in leadership when the audience calls for it.
  • Build product and industry knowledge as you ramp, and keep current on threats, competitors, and the SentinelOne platform.
  • Respond quickly to internal and external requests, and deliver on what you promised.

What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring?

Ideal candidates will have:

  • 2 to 3 years of successful sales performance at SentinelOne or a comparable or more complex cybersecurity company, hitting and over-achieving quota in a segment equal to or greater than SMB.
  • General industry understanding and high-level product knowledge. You know what endpoint security is and what it is for. Deeper expertise is welcome but not required; you will learn the products and the industry as you onboard.
  • Channel network or reseller experience is a plus.
  • Some experience creating, maintaining, and executing a territory plan.
  • Proven ability to convert intent into result through deliberate action.
  • Open and ready to learn, able to take honest feedback, and eager to work with leadership and peers.
  • Proactive, communicative, and solution-oriented when something is not working for you or your teammates.
  • Professional, driven, collaborative, and honest. You look out for your peers.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.
  • Proficiency with Salesforce, Clari, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, and Salesloft.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.

Why SentinelOne?

AI is redefining how the world operates and rewriting the rules of security in real time, and SentinelOne was built for this moment. From day one, we architected an AI-native platform designed to operate at machine speed, not as an add-on to legacy systems but as the foundation itself. If you want to build where innovation and impact move together, this is that place.

We invest in our Sentinels with comprehensive, competitive benefits designed to support you and your family:

Equity & Rewards

  • Restricted Stock Units (RSUs)
  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)

Time Off & Wellbeing

  • Flexible time off

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage

Work Perks & Flexibility

  • Home office allowance
  • Mobile phone reimbursement

Wellness & Lifestyle

  • Wellness coach

  • Fertility coverage
  • Adoption & surrogacy reimbursement

Clinical Research Associate - Canada

Syneos Health® is a leading fully integrated biopharmaceutical solutions organization built to accelerate customer success. We translate unique clinical, medical affairs and commercial insights into outcomes to address modern market realities.

Our Clinical Development model brings the customer and the patient to the center of everything that we do. We are continuously looking for ways to simplify and streamline our work to not only make Syneos Health easier to work with, but to make us easier to work for.

Whether you join us in a Functional Service Provider partnership or a Full-Service environment, you’ll collaborate with passionate problem solvers, innovating as a team to help our customers achieve their goals. We are agile and driven to accelerate the delivery of therapies, because we are passionate to change lives.

Discover what our 29,000 employees, across 110 countries already know:

WORK HERE MATTERS EVERYWHERE

Why Syneos Health

  • We are passionate about developing our people, through career development and progression; supportive and engaged line management; technical and therapeutic area training; peer recognition and total rewards program.
  • We are committed to our Total Self culture – where you can authentically be yourself. Our Total Self culture is what unites us globally, and we are dedicated to taking care of our people.
  • We are continuously building the company we all want to work for and our customers want to work with. Why? Because when we bring together diversity of thoughts, backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives – we’re able to create a place where everyone feels like they belong.

Job Responsibilities

  • Performs site qualification, site initiation, interim monitoring, site management and close-out visits (performed on-site or remotely) ensuring regulatory, ICH-GCP and/or Good Pharmacoepidemiology Practice (GPP) and protocol compliance. Uses judgment and experience to evaluate overall performance of site and site staff and to provide recommendations regarding site-specific actions; immediately communicates/escalates serious issues to the project team and develops action plans. Maintains a working knowledge of ICH/GCP Guidelines or other applicable guidance, relevant regulations, and company SOPs/processes.
  • Verifies the process of obtaining informed consent has been adequately performed and documented for each subject/patient as required/appropriate. Demonstrates diligence in protecting the confidentiality of each subject/patient. Assesses factors that might affect subject/patient’s safety and clinical data integrity at an investigator/physician site such as protocol deviation/violations and pharmacovigilance issues.
  • Per the Clinical Monitoring/Site Management Plan (CMP/SMP): Assesses site processes. Conducts Source Document Review of appropriate site source documents and medical records. Verifies required clinical data entered in the case report form (CRF) is accurate and complete via review of site source documents and medical records. Applies query resolution techniques remotely and on site, and provides guidance to site staff as necessary, driving query resolution to closure within agreed timelines. Utilizes available hardware and software to support the effective conduct of the clinical study data review and capture. Verifies site compliance with electronic data capture requirements
  • May perform investigational product (IP) inventory, reconciliation and reviews storage and security. Verifies the IP has been dispensed and administered to subjects/patients according to the protocol. Verifies issues or risks associated with blinded or randomized information related to IP. Applies knowledge of GCP/local regulations and organizational procedures to ensure IP is appropriately (re)labelled, imported and released/returned.
  • Routinely reviews the Investigator Site File (ISF) for accuracy, timeliness and completeness. Reconciles contents of the ISF with the Trial Master File (TMF). Ensures the investigator/physician site is aware of the requirement of archiving essential documents in accordance with local guidelines and regulations.
  • Documents activities via confirmation letters, follow-up letters, trip reports, communication logs, and other required project documents as per SOPs and Clinical Monitoring Plan/Site Management Plan. Supports subject/patient recruitment, retention and awareness strategies. Enters data into tracking systems as required to track all observations, ongoing status and assigned action items to resolution.
  • Understands project scope, budgets, and timelines for own and others’ activities in the clinical team; manages site-level activities / communication to ensure project objectives, deliverables and timelines are met. Must be able to quickly adapt to changing priorities to achieve goals / targets.
  • May act as primary liaison with project site personnel, or in collaboration with Central Monitoring Associate. Ensures all assigned sites and project-specific site team members are trained and compliant with applicable requirements.
  • Prepares for and attends Investigator Meetings and/or sponsor face to face meetings. Participates, and may, with supervision, lead, global clinical monitoring/project staff meetings (inclusive of Sponsor representation, as applicable) and attends clinical training sessions according to the project specific requirements.
  • Provides guidance at the site and project level towards audit readiness standards and supports preparation for audit and required follow-up actions.
  • May provide training or mentorship to more junior level CRAs. May perform training and sign off visits for junior CRA staff, as assigned.
  • May be mentored and assigned clinical operations lead tasks under supervision of an experienced Clinical Operations Lead (COL), or operational line manager. For Real World Late Phase (RWLP), the Sr. CRA I will use the business card title of Sr. Site Management Associate I. Additional responsibilities include:Site support throughout the study lifecycle from site identification through close out
    Knowledge of local requirements for real world late phase study designs
    Chart abstraction activities and data collection
    As required, collaborate and build relationships with Sponsor and other affiliates, medical science liaisons and local country staff
    Identify and communicate out of scope activities to Lead CRA/Project Manager
    Proactively suggest potential sites based on local knowledge of treatment patterns, patient advocacy and Health Care Provider (HCP) associations
    Identify operational efficiencies and process improvements
    Develop country level informed consent forms
    Collaborate with RWLP Regulatory team to ensure updated regulatory information is applied and shared
    Participate in bid defense meetings

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or RN in a related field or equivalent combination of education, training and experience
  • Knowledge of Good Clinical Practice/ICH Guidelines and other applicable regulatory requirements
  • Must demonstrate good computer skills and be able to embrace new technologies
  • Excellent communication, presentation and interpersonal skills. Basic level of critical thinking skills expected.
  • Ability to manage required travel of up to 75% on a regular basis

We are always excited to connect with great talent. This posting is intended for a [possible] upcoming opportunity rather than a live role. By expressing your interest, you'll be added to our talent pipeline and considered should this role become available.

Get to know Syneos Health

Over the past 5 years, we have worked with 94% of all Novel FDA Approved Drugs, 95% of EMA Authorized Products and over 200 Studies across 73,000 Sites and 675,000+ Trial patients.

No matter what your role is, you’ll take the initiative and challenge the status quo with us in a highly competitive and ever-changing environment. Learn more about Syneos Health.

Additional Information

Tasks, duties, and responsibilities as listed in this job description are not exhaustive. The Company, at its sole discretion and with no prior notice, may assign other tasks, duties, and job responsibilities. Equivalent experience, skills, and/or education will also be considered so qualifications of incumbents may differ from those listed in the Job Description.   • Owns the roadmap for a defined platform area end to end, from problem framing through release and adoption measurement, and can defend the rationale behind every item on it
  • Identifies the most impactful problems to solve within the area, including foundational platform work that is not immediately visible to customers, and makes the case for that investment with evidence
  • Defines the requirements for shared identity, entitlement, and access services so that licensing, session, and permission behavior is consistent and enforceable across Revu, web, and mobile
  • Advances the security posture of the owned area, partnering with security and engineering on permission models, access controls, and remediation, and weighing customer impact against risk

  • Builds the administrative and account-management workflows enterprise customers depend on to deploy, govern, and secure Bluebeam at scale, improving adoption, conversion, and retention in support of Bluebeam Max

raw.description:
Retrieval Operations Lead

Remote

About Reveleer

Reveleer delivers a unified platform spanning risk adjustment, quality improvement, clinical intelligence, and member management for health plans and provider organizations navigating the complexity of value-based care. Trusted by 80+ customer organizations nationwide, the platform integrates data, analytics, and intelligent workflow automation into one governed system designed to support traceable documentation across diagnoses, quality measures, and submissions. With regulatory expertise and transparent, human-in-the-loop AI at its core, Reveleer supports organizations working to advance care quality, strengthen documentation integrity, and sustain the operational readiness needed to navigate audits with confidence.

POSITION OVERVIEW:

The Retrieval Lead drives frontline execution of Reveleer's retrieval program, covering approximately 500,000 chases beginning with the October 2026 go-live.

This role owns the day-to-day relationship with the program's largest AIDs, distributes and rebalances chase work assignments across the PSR team, and trains new and existing PSRs on retrieval workflows, standard processes, and provider outreach best practices.

This role is the first line of response for provider escalations, resolving access and outreach issues directly and escalating only what requires the Retrieval Manager's involvement.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

Large AID Relationship & Provider Contact

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for a program's highest-volume AIDs, maintaining direct relationships with provider office staff.
  • Monitor retrieval performance for large AIDs and proactively address barriers before they affect chase completion.
  • Coordinate directly with provider offices on record request logistics, portal access, and recurring retrieval issues.

Work Assignment & Queue Management

  • Distribute and rebalance daily chase assignments across the PSR team based on AID priority, chase age, and retrieval deadlines.
  • Monitor individual PSR workloads and adjust assignments to keep the queue moving and prevent aged chases from stalling.
  • Partner with the Retrieval Manager on weekly volume planning and flag capacity gaps before they affect throughput.

PSR Training & Development

  • Onboard and train new PSRs on chase workflows, AID ownership, pend code handling, and platform agent hand-offs.
  • Deliver ongoing coaching and refreshers on retrieval best practices, call quality, and documentation standards.
  • Maintain training materials and job aids, updating them as workflows or systems change.

Provider Escalation Management

  • Own first-line resolution of provider escalations related to retrieval outreach, record requests, or access issues.
  • Document escalation patterns and root causes and recommend workflow or script changes that reduce recurring issues.
  • Escalate unresolved or systemic provider issues to the Retrieval Manager with a clear summary and recommend next step.

Performance Monitoring & Coaching

  • Track individual and team-level retrieval rate, pend rate, and productivity against program targets.
  • Provide day-to-day feedback and coaching to PSRs based on chase outcomes and call quality.
  • Flag underperformance or training gaps to the Retrieval Manager and support corrective action plans.

Process Adherence & Documentation

  • Ensure PSR adherence to standard retrieval processes, procedures, and documentation requirements.
  • Maintain accurate, current records on AID assignments, escalation status, and chase ownership.
  • Support the Retrieval Manager with input on process updates and standard operating procedure revisions.

ABOUT YOU:

  • 2+ years of experience in healthcare operations, chart retrieval, risk adjustment, or HEDIS/quality program support.
  • 1+ years of experience training, coaching, or leading the daily work of other individual contributors.
  • Working knowledge of risk adjustment and HEDIS retrieval workflows, including chase, AID, and pend code concepts.
  • Experience managing provider-facing communication, including resolving access or outreach escalations directly.
  • Strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage and rebalance work assignments across a team in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proficiency in Excel and comfort working within chase or case management systems.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience delivering training or coaching.

Preferred

  • Direct experience supporting Medicare Advantage or ACA health plan retrieval programs.
  • Prior experience formally training or onboarding new hires in a call center or retrieval operations setting.

WHAT YOU’LL RECEIVE:

•Competitive salary 

•• Medical, Dental and Vision benefits 

•• 401k match

•• Generous PTO plan 

  •  Our compensation reflects the cost of labor across several US geographic markets. Pay is based on several factors including market location and may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

•Reveleer E-Verifies all new hires.

  • Reveleer is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or genetic information, in compliance with applicable federal, state and local law.
Salary: $21 – $28 / hour

WHO WE ARE:

Ltd., develops, manufactures, and markets innovative imaging technologies and is committed to delivering fast, easy, and accurate diagnostic solutions to healthcare providers. Boston Imaging is the US headquarters for sales, marketing, service and distribution of all Samsung digital radiography and ultrasound systems. Our advanced medical technologies are used worldwide in leading healthcare institutions, helping providers enhance patient care, improve patient satisfaction, and increase workflow efficiency. Samsung is committed to being a leader in the field of healthcare imaging.
Samsung is a growing presence in the radiology field and is committed to delivering fast, easy and accurate imaging solutions to healthcare providers. The full range of Samsung imaging solutions includes Ultrasound, Digital Radiography, and mobile Computed Tomography (mCT). Samsung aims to become a global leader in the medical imaging space and is investing heavily in developing innovative, advanced imaging technologies that will improve the quality of people's lives.
Samsung keeps a constant eye on the always-evolving, ever-changing imaging industry. By continually enhancing current product lines and seeking to develop new technologies, Samsung is at the forefront of the imaging frontier.

ROLE DESCRIPTION:

Responsible for escalated onsite support for our premium ultrasound imaging products within the tier one hospital networks; Represent Samsung as the subject matter expert in Ultrasound and serve as the “go to” resource for difficult service issues; This position is remote and/or office based. This position works from an assigned strategic region within the United States supporting Samsung channel partners and end users; Develop strong relationships with the end users and participate in the sale of both new systems and service contracts. This position is unique requiring both highly technical skills and participation in the sales process, it is both tactical and strategic, which will be essential to the success of the sales growth of high-end ultrasound products. This position will also be responsible for providing direction and assistance to “generalist” field service engineers either contracted or direct/dealer employees.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include the following. Other duties may be assigned

  • Serve as customer facing senior technical resource and work in collaboration with biomed engineers and other senior staff members at the tier one hospitals

  • On-site troubleshooting and resolving complex technical problems on Ultrasound equipment in a medical environment

  • Have a very high level of product knowledge
  • Build a service data base of information to align with our corrective action systems
  • Run tests and simulations at our facility to assist with problem solving
  • Travel to the field to train and or resolve customer issues
  • Attend and complete all required training and certification exams
  • Learn to be proficient in service and repair of all systems (current, new, and updates)
  • Be able to work independently and take ownership of customer base
  • Be completely self-sufficient in the field
  • Manage time effectively; prioritize and make good business judgments and decisions in relationship to efficiency, effectiveness while meeting daily service expectations
  • Become and remain compliant with any required credentialing services (this includes, but is not limited to, passing a drug screen(s) and background check(s))
  • Follow all company policies regarding travel, expenses, meetings, and meals
  • Maintain basic system operational and service understanding in order to answer customer questions and resolve issues independently
  • Maintain service calendar accessible by CS Manager/staff
  • Close reports to CSD on Great Plains, PM Reports, Service Reports
  • Required to wear dosimeter when in direct contact with radiation emitting devices

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

  • Technical degree in electrical or software engineering, or other related discipline or equivalent experience preferred
  • 10 plus years in field service preferred
  • Exceptional customer service skills with expertise in troubleshooting, diagnosing and solving complex technical issues
  • Must be able to be compliant with hospital credentialing requirements
  • Wide degree of creativity, leadership, and latitude is expected
  • Relevant and demonstrable technical support service experience in the Ultrasound environment
  • Strong working knowledge of Ultrasound hardware and software operating systems
  • Ability to work professionally with all levels of hospital organization staff
  • Excellent organizational, time management, written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to complete multiple tasks with minimal direction
  • Ability to travel 75% of the time
  • ISO, FDA, CMDR Awareness Training and Product Complaint System, or Certification – Health Stream
  • Experience with mechanical devices, tools and test equipment, telecommunications systems, and working knowledge of computer networking
  • Must demonstrate fluent English verbal and written communication skills and work effectively in a demanding, fast paced environment
  • Willing to travel overnight
  • Valid driving license and satisfactory driving record is mandatory and background and drug testing (pre and post-employment) is required
  • Budget, expense, and resource management experience required
  • Must be able to assemble facts from various areas, analyze data, and provide informed recommendations to management Position is administered in an extremely fluid, fast paced, at time high pressure, with multiple high priority demands.
  • The employee is exposed to various business environments such as: extremely busy hospitals or clinics where down time creates stress for the business and the patient

COMPUTER SKILLS

  • You must be comfortable with technology, and be able demonstrate proficiency with MS Office package, including Excel, Word, and PowerPoint, as well as Outlook, Internet Explorer, and Google Chrome

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Regularly lift and /or move up to 25 pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to 40-60 pounds
  • Frequently required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl and talk or hear

COMPETENCIES

  • Ability to organize and prioritize tasks resulting in consistent productivity
  • Ability to function within and support a team environment and build strong working relationships
  • Dependable and punctual

Located North of Boston in Danvers, MA, NeuroLogica Corporation, who does business in the Ultrasound and Digital Radiography space as Boston Imaging, is a subsidiary of Samsung Electronics who develops, manufactures and markets innovative medical imaging equipment for healthcare facilities and private practices worldwide. raw.description:
Legal Counsel (m/f/d)

Remote Europe

Hello 👋 I’m Robert, Finance & Legal Lead at Kayzen and I’m now looking for a Legal Counsel to join our team. As we scale our business globally — managing an increasingly complex client and vendor landscape, navigating cross-border data privacy requirements, and growing our equity and corporate structure — we need a sharp, pragmatic, and commercially minded legal mind to own our legal function. You will take what we have built so far and professionalise, scale, and strengthen it. Working closely with our Finance & Legal Lead, you will be a true business partner to senior leadership across the company.

About Kayzen

Kayzen is an App demand-side platform (DSP) dedicated to democratizing app advertising on Mobile and Connected TV devices. We enable leading apps, agencies, media buyers, and brands to run programmatic customer acquisition, retargeting, and brand performance campaigns through our self-serve and managed service options. Built on the three core pillars of performance, transparency, and control, Kayzen powers the world’s best performance marketing teams with bespoke solutions that fuel business growth and deliver a competitive advantage. With an unprecedented scale of 300B+ daily ad requests from 1.6B+ unique users worldwide, we serve up to 1B+ ads per day in 180 countries. Kayzen is accessible through our APIs and user interface.

The team

You will join a small, senior team and work directly alongside our Finance & Legal Lead. Your key stakeholders will be the leadership team, as well as our Finance, Operations, and Commercial functions across a globally distributed organisation.

The role

As Legal Counsel, you will be Kayzen’s primary legal owner across four core areas. You will operate as a trusted business partner — not just a gatekeeper — and are expected to move fast, apply sound commercial judgment, and help the business scale without unnecessary legal friction.

Responsibilities

GDPR & data privacy compliance

  • Own and continuously develop Kayzen’s GDPR compliance programme as an AdTech company operating across multiple jurisdictions, with a particular focus on EU and US privacy frameworks
  • Advise on data processing agreements, privacy notices, consent frameworks, and cross-border data transfers
  • Act as primary point of contact for internal privacy questions

Transaction advice & contract negotiations

  • Provide legal counsel on T&Cs and related transactions
  • Lead or support contract negotiations with clients and vendors, including MSAs, SaaS agreements, partnership agreements, and NDAs
  • Ensure commercial contracts are legally robust and aligned with company risk appetite

Cap table & corporate law

  • Manage and maintain Kayzen’s cap table
  • Oversee corporate governance across Kayzen’s group structure, including subsidiary management, shareholder resolutions, and notarial filings under German law
  • Support fundraising and investor relations from a legal and corporate perspective

General compliance

  • Further develop and scale Kayzen’s compliance framework to match our growth as an internationally operating company
  • Monitor relevant regulatory developments (ad-tech, data privacy, employment, corporate) and translate them into actionable guidance for the business

Requirements

  • Qualified lawyer (“Volljurist”) or Business lawyer (“Wirtschaftsjurist”) with 2–5 years of relevant professional experience
  • Strong understanding of German business law is essential; additionally solid understanding of international and US legal frameworks, particularly in the context of data privacy and commercial contracts
  • Strong knowledge of GDPR and European data protection law; familiarity with US privacy regulations (CCPA etc.) a strong plus
  • Experience in a start-up or scale-up environment is strongly preferred — you know how to work lean, move fast, and prioritise pragmatically
  • Hands-on experience with contract drafting and commercial negotiations across a variety of agreement types
  • Familiarity with cap table management and corporate governance in a VC-backed or founder-led company context
  • Commercially minded: you understand that good legal advice enables business, not just protects it
  • Fluent in English & German
  • Demonstrated ability to leverage AI tools to enhance legal productivity — you move fast and work smart

What we offer

  • A high-impact legal role with real ownership and room to grow the function
  • Direct collaboration with the Finance & Legal Lead and senior leadership
  • Competitive fixed compensation commensurate with experience
  • Fully remote work arrangement
  • €500 home-office setup budget
  • €1,000 annual learning & development budget
  • A motivated, diverse, and internationally distributed team

Our Internal Games Team is focused on working on games that we as Gamebreaking own and are in charge of creating either independently or in partnership with a publisher.

At Gamebreaking, helping the growth of our interns is a top priority. We have a strong history of our interns being successful in the games industry both inside and outside of Gamebreaking. You will be paired with a highly experienced mentor to help guide your development throughout the program, as well as managerial resources to get you all the support you may need. We want to bring people onto our team who are hungry to grow and excited to make a big impact.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet all of the skills listed here. We understand that your qualifications may shine through in different ways and can be based on unique perspectives and experiences.

Gamebreaking Studios is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity, and are committed to maintaining a safe and inclusive environment for our team.

We do not use AI to screen our candidates, and we encourage you not to use AI as part of your application or cover letter so your personality can shine!

Duration and Employment Status

We are a fully remote working environment seeking current students, recent graduates ~1 year out of universities, or those with similar experience to join our company. This is an entry-level position with no prior work experience required, though candidates with prior work experience will be considered.

This position is a paid internship between 3 and 6 months duration, with the possibility of a direct hire to full-time at its conclusion. We seek a candidate able to work a minimum of 30 hours per week, with a preference for 40 hours. Candidates must be able to start work no later than January 12th, 2027. Otherwise, the duration and timeframe of this internship are flexible depending on the candidate and their situation.

Benefits and employment duration may differ based on student status and country-specific laws

Desired Skills & Qualifications

  • A passion for games and entertainment that shows. Whether you love video games, board games, cosplay, or freeze tag — we want to know! If it doesn’t shine through your resume (e.g. work, academic, or community experience), please submit a cover letter.
  • 2+ years of experience in your discipline (academic or demonstrable personal projects are acceptable)
  • Enrolled in, or recently graduated from, a university program or an equivalent program focused on Game Development or equivalent.
  • Self-motivated and willing to work in multiple areas of game development
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills

Pluses

  • Worked on a game project with a team of developers before
  • Any showable game projects, or portfolios of your work

Your responsibilities

  • Be hungry to learn and grow
  • Show strong initiative when planning and executing your tasks.
  • Clearly communicate progress on tasks with other team members
  • Regularly contribute to team meetings and rituals.
  • Speak up and improve our company culture where possible!

Our Responsibilities to You

  • Encourage healthy working hours, PTO, and a respect for your time
  • Foster an environment of equal opportunity, treatment, and inclusion
  • Create a fun and playful environment that remains professional and respectful
  • Grow our culture positively and meaningfully through a high level of transparency and thoughtful conversation
  • Provide opportunities and support for you to learn and grow

About Gamebreaking

Gamebreaking Studios is a young, growing, LA-based company founded by technology leaders from around games, entertainment, and software. We found early success providing work-for-hire to other studios and now build everything from end-to-end games to online game platforms to individual feature integrations. We also develop our own games and IP alongside other projects.

Our mission: We aspire to make games and media so fun that it improves people's relationships and behaviors. We believe that making fun-first games enables us to have a positive impact. We believe deeply in our core values and hope to find people who share them:

  • Take Responsibility
  • Raise The Tide, Not One Boat
  • Ambitious Goals, Disciplined Execution
  • Design For People, Own Your Craft
  • We Play Together

Working at Gamebreaking as a non-US citizen

This position is open to candidates living and working in Latin America. Applicants must be fluent in English, willing to work according to US time zones (must be available 8am - 3pm Pacific Time), and have a strong, stable internet connection conducive to remote work and video calls. Outside the US, we work with an Employer of Record ( to hire employees and contractors.

description: GROW WITH US: Tandem Diabetes Care creates new possibilities for people living with diabetes, their loved ones, and their healthcare providers through a positively different experience.

raw.title: Demand Planner Manager
raw.excerpt: GROW WITH US: Tandem Diabetes Care creates new possibilities for people living with diabetes, their loved ones, and their healthcare providers through a positively different experience.
raw.description:
GROW WITH US: Tandem Diabetes Care creates new possibilities for people living with diabetes, their loved ones, and their healthcare providers through a positively different experience. We’d love for you to team up with us to “innovate every day,” put “people first,” and take the “no-shortcuts” approach that has propelled us to become a leader in the diabetes technology industry.

STAY AWESOME: Tandem Diabetes Care is proud to manufacture and sell the Tandem Mobi system and t:slim X2 insulin pump with Control-IQ+ technology — an advanced predictive algorithm that automates insulin delivery. But we’re so much more than that. Our company’s human-centered approach to design, development, and support delivers innovative products and services for people who use insulin. Because many of our own team members live with type 1 diabetes, or have a loved one impacted by diabetes, the work is personal, and we are committed to the cause. Learn more at tandemdiabetes.com

A DAY IN THE LIFE:

At Tandem Diabetes Care, we are creating new possibilities for people living with diabetes, their loved ones, and healthcare providers through a positively different experience.

We are looking for a Demand Planer Manager to join our International team. This role is based in the Netherlands and offers a remote working arrangement. The successful candidate should be willing and able to travel regularly to other international locations as required to support business needs.
In this influential role, you will lead demand planning, forecasting, inventory allocation, and operational coordination across Tandem’s international distributor and direct markets. You will help align customer demand, product availability, revenue expectations, and fulfilment plans while strengthening the processes and partnerships that support our continued international growth.

STAY AWESOME:

Tandem is dedicated to making diabetes technology more intuitive, innovative, and human. We combine advanced technology with a personal connection to our mission, always keeping the needs of people living with diabetes at the heart of what we do.

As our Demand Planer Manager, you will turn market insights and commercial priorities into clear, actionable demand plans. Working across Commercial, Supply Chain, Finance, Operations, Marketing, Regulatory, and distributor partners, you will help identify risks early, optimise inventory, and ensure international markets are ready for product launches and changing customer needs.

A DAY IN THE LIFE:

In this role, you will:

  • Own the monthly demand planning and forecasting process for Tandem’s international distributor partners and direct markets.

  • Consolidate market forecasts and analyse forecast accuracy, bias, demand variability, purchasing patterns, and emerging trends.

  • Establish effective planning rhythms, including monthly reviews with direct markets and quarterly demand reviews with distributor partners.

  • Lead and participate in S&OP discussions covering demand, inventory health, service levels, purchasing patterns, and operational risks.

  • Build strong partnerships with country leadership and distributor teams to gather real-time market intelligence, commercial insights, competitive developments, tender opportunities, and launch information.

  • Challenge assumptions and investigate material forecast changes, demand spikes, demand erosion, inventory imbalances, and unusual ordering trends.

  • Create consensus demand plans that balance market expectations, inventory availability, supply constraints, financial objectives, and operational capabilities.

  • Align forecasts with open orders, shipment plans, product availability, and fulfilment expectations in partnership with Operations Specialists, Logistics, Fulfilment, and Supply Chain.

  • Support new product introductions, software releases, product enhancements, and discontinuations by developing market-specific forecasts, inventory strategies, and transition plans.

  • Identify ageing, excess, or potentially obsolete inventory and work with international markets to develop mitigation and depletion strategies.

  • Lead demand allocation planning during supply-constrained situations, taking account of customer impact, tender commitments, launches, available inventory, and market requirements.

  • Partner with Finance on revenue planning and help develop dashboards and reporting covering forecast performance, inventory exposure, order trends, and revenue projections.

  • Present demand, inventory, and fulfilment insights to Commercial and Operations leadership.

  • Improve planning tools, reporting, operational workflows, automation, and analytics to increase forecast accuracy and operational efficiency.

  • Provide leadership, coaching, development, and performance management to Operations Specialists.

  • Set team priorities, support cross-training and succession planning, and create a culture of collaboration, customer focus, and continuous improvement.

The position may require flexibility to collaborate across international time zones and independent international travel of up to 25%.

EXTRA AWESOME:

You will bring:

  • A bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Business, Operations Management, Finance, or a related field.

  • At least six years of experience in demand planning, supply chain planning, sales operations, inventory planning, or commercial operations.

  • Strong knowledge of forecasting, demand planning, inventory management, allocation, and supply chain processes.

  • Advanced analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with the confidence to assess complex supply-and-demand scenarios and make data-informed recommendations.

  • Financial and commercial acumen, including an understanding of revenue forecasting.

  • Experience collaborating across Commercial, Finance, Operations, and Supply Chain functions.

  • Strong communication, presentation, influencing, and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to communicate insights to leadership audiences.

  • Fluent spoken and written English.

  • The ability to manage multiple priorities in an international, fast-moving, and evolving environment.

It would be especially valuable if you also have:

  • Experience supporting international markets, distributors, or complex fulfilment networks.

  • Experience working in a global or distributor-based commercial organisation.

  • Familiarity with CRM, ERP, order-management, Salesforce, or Microsoft Dynamics environments.

  • Experience supporting product launches, lifecycle transitions, inventory allocation, or constrained-supply planning.

  • Experience leading, coaching, and developing operational team members.

  • Fluency in an additional European language.

If your experience does not match every point, we still encourage you to apply. We value transferable skills, different perspectives, and the potential to grow.

WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU?

You will join an international, high-tech MedTech environment where your work will directly influence product availability and operational performance across multiple markets.

You can expect stimulating work in an innovative field, meaningful autonomy, excellent working conditions, and the opportunity to collaborate with motivated colleagues across Tandem’s international organisation. You will also have the opportunity to shape scalable planning practices, strengthen team capabilities, and contribute to successful product launches and international growth.

WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE:
At Tandem, we believe joy fuels excellence. That's why we've built a workplace that celebrates your achievements and supports your well-being. Our team thrives on pushing boundaries and fostering growth, all while maintaining a spirit of fun and camaraderie. This is just one of the ways we stay awesome!

BE YOU, WITH US!

We embrace the value that every single one of us brings to the table. But sometimes we forget that when we don’t meet 100% of a job description’s criteria – maybe you’re feeling that way right now? We encourage you to apply anyway. Because we want you to be you, with us.

Tandem is firmly committed to being an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, disability, sex, race, religion or belief, gender identity or expression, marriage/civil partnership, pregnancy/maternity, or sexual orientation. We are an inclusive organization, and we welcome applications from a wide range of candidates. Selection for roles will be based on individual merit alone.

REFERRALS:
We love a good referral! If you know someone who would be a great fit for this position, please share!

Make a move that matters. Join Tandem Diabetes Care, where we're turning challenges into triumphs every day and where your talents will help shape a healthier, happier tomorrow.

The Central Monitoring Associate position is responsible for providing support to the clinical monitoring teams while utilizing centralized data and reporting tools in accordance with Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Regulatory requirements, ICH and GCP guidelines and study specific plans.

Essential Functions:

  • Performs remote site monitoring and management activities for assigned project(s) in accordance with FDA and/or local regulations and guidelines, ICH GCPs and ProPharma Group SOPs and project plans.

  • Supports collection of data, and report generation to support activities such as recruitment plan, and enrollment, drug supply status, site payment status, and any other relevant tracking to support successful clinical trial execution.
  • Supports data risk assessments as assigned.
  • Supports monitoring teams throughout the duration of the study including communication with the clinical site institutions as appropriate.
  • May be required to support any document collection, visit preparation, and study data review and central monitoring activities as assigned.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Necessary Skills and Abilities:

  • Effective communication, and interpersonal skills with ability to partner with cross functional internal and external stakeholders.
  • Must be able to prioritize multiple tasks, plan proactively, and accomplish goals using well-defined instructions and procedures.
  • Ability to contribute to the development of tools and processes that increase measured efficiencies of the project.
  • Proficiency in working with systems used in the clinical trial execution such as but not limited to Electronic Document Management Systems, Electronic Data Capture Systems, Clinical Trial Management Systems, etc.
  • Exhibits a good understanding of general quality assurance concepts and practices.
  • Highly organized with a strong attention to detail.

Educational Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred. Persons without a formal degree who have comparable depth and breadth of training and experience and who meet job-specific criteria are eligible for consideration.

Experience Requirements:

  • Minimum 3 years of experience in study coordination and in house monitoring, or relevant work experience in the Biotechnology or Pharmaceutical industries or relevant, regulated environment.

raw.description:
About the Role

Abnormal AI is seeking a Product Manager (Outbound) who builds the field motion from the ground up for every new product launched. There is no universal playbook, no inherited demo flow, and no proven messaging to hand off. Each new product requires its own: this person architects it, validates it in close partnership with the field, and hands off a repeatable motion the field can run at scale before moving to the next product launch.

Outbound Product Management (OPM) is R&D's operating layer in the field, the function that sits between what we build and how it performs with customers. That means being first in on a new product, before anyone has figured out how to sell or demo it, running structured validation across customer accounts, and distinguishing a product gap from a positioning or sales-motion gap. You'll work in close partnership with Product Management and Product Marketing—OPM owns the field motion, not the roadmap, but the pattern analysis and positioning work you bring back is what keeps both teams calibrated to what's actually happening with customers.

This is not a feedback-intake role. You'll be operating on products that don't have established answers yet — the messaging is still being proven, the competitive positioning is still being tested, and the product itself may still be taking shape. You'll know when a read is solid enough to bring back to the cross-functional team versus when it needs more digging, and you'll drive the motion forward without waiting for someone to hand you a map.

What You'll Do

  • Architect the field motion for an assigned product launch: design how the product gets demoed, how a POV gets structured, and what the field needs to run it at scale — then get hands-on with customer discovery, deep dives, and POVs to validate the approach.
  • Test and refine messaging hypotheses in live deals alongside Sales Engineers, and diagnose competitive loss reasons.
  • Brief PM with pattern analysis across accounts, distinguishing a product gap from a positioning or sales-motion problem.
  • Partner with Product Marketing as a standing collaborator, stress-testing messaging in live deals and reporting what's landing versus what needs to change.
  • Own the handoff at General Availability: document what worked, what broke, and what the field needs to run the motion independently — then move to the next product and do it again.

Must-Have Skills

  • 5+ years in Product Management or Solutions/Sales Engineering in enterprise security.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently synthesize unfamiliar products quickly — given a new product and limited context, you can identify what matters, form a hypothesis, and start building the field motion: how the product gets demoed, how a POV gets structured, and what the field needs to run it at scale.
  • Experience working in a pre-launch or early-stage product environment before a playbook existed, with a specific program, motion, or deliverable built from scratch to show for it.
  • Credibility that speaks through work and presence, and the instinct to move toward problems before they're assigned.
  • Strong written and verbal communication; credible in front of technical buyers and security teams, equally comfortable in a live customer conversation and an internal roadmap review.
  • High operational excellence and ownership: you've taken a field observation from raw signal to a documented recommendation that a PM or GTM team acted on.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the capacity to reason through ambiguous problems and move to a working hypothesis without waiting for the full picture.

Nice to Have

  • Prior involvement in new product launches, design partnerships, early-access, and/or beta programs.
  • Experience running or presenting in structured cross-functional forums (POV reviews, launch/GTM syncs).
  • Familiarity with enterprise security platforms such as CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Zscaler, Wiz, Microsoft, or similar.
  • Comfort using AI tools to synthesize patterns across large sets of qualitative input (support tickets, call transcripts, win/loss notes).
  • Prior startup experience.

Why This Role Matters

This role is a career inflection point. It’s a senior seat with real organizational weight that will set a new standard for the team around you. The people who thrive here carry credibility on arrival—they've been in enough high-stakes customer and cross-functional environments that they don't need to win the room before the work begins. If you come from a product management background, this is where you build the GTM fluency that traditional PM roles don't give you, and that fluency is increasingly what separates good product people from exceptional ones. If you come from a solutions engineering background, this is where technical credibility becomes strategic ownership. Either way, you'll be at the frontier of what we're building, working on products that don't have all the answers yet, shaping the motion before anyone else has, and coming out the other side with a profile that's genuinely hard to replicate elsewhere. The launches you'll be working on aren't side bets—they're the company's biggest bets for our next phase of growth, and this role is at the center of bringing them to market.

Actual compensation will be determined based on several non-discriminatory factors including skills, experience, qualifications, and geographic location.
In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for bonus or incentive compensation, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package.
